On a 1 to 100 chart, Mawuli from Hohoe covers the number just below 52 with a groundnut shell. Which number did he cover? Which number is just above 52?
Abena's teacher in Sunyani hides one number on the 1 to 100 chart. It is between 69 and 71. Which number is it? Which number sits right under it?

math:B1.1.1.1.3.text: Use your hand-span to measure your desk, as Kwame does at his school in Koforidua. Count the hand-spans. How many hand-spans long is the desk?
Azara fills a small bucket with a cup at a borehole in Walewale. Try it too. Count each cup you pour. How many cups fill the bucket?
Nii walks heel to toe across his classroom in Teshie and counts his steps. Do the same in your room. How many of your feet long is it?

math:B1.1.1.1.4.text: Esi has 14 mangoes at Mankessim market. Kojo has 9 mangoes. Match them one to one. Who has more? Who has less?
Three trotros leave Kaneshie. One has 12 people, one has 20 and one has 15. Put the numbers in order from least to most.
Dery has 39 cashew nuts in Wa. His sister has 1 more. How many has she? Their friend has 1 less than Dery. How many is that?

math:B1.1.1.1.5.text: Adwoa sold 27 balls of kenkey in Winneba. Tetteh sold 32. Write the two numbers with >, < or = between them.
Class 1A in Zuarungu has 45 pupils. Class 1B also has 45. Put the right sign between the numbers: 45 __ 45.
In ampe at a school in Keta, Selorm's team has 18 points. Enyonam's team has 14. Write 18 __ 14 with >, < or =. Then say it in words.

math:B1.1.1.1.6.text: Akosua has 12 bofrot at a stall in Nkawkaw. Yakubu has 8. Tell two true things about the numbers 12 and 8.
A hen in Navrongo has 6 chicks. Draw a group of groundnuts that has more than 6. Draw another group that has fewer than 6.
Three friends thread beads in Odumase Krobo. Kekeli has 50. Naa has 48. Akolgo has 5. Whose number is a little less than 50? Whose number is a lot less?

math:B1.1.2.1.1.text: Afia has 9 groundnuts. Her mother in Ejisu gives her 6 more. Act it out with stones. How many groundnuts has Afia now?
There are 17 pupils on a school bus in Tema. 5 get off at the first stop. How many are still on the bus?
Atanga had 13 guinea fowl eggs. He sold 4 at Bolgatanga market. Do you add or take away to find what is left? How many are left?

math:B1.1.2.2.1.text: Kafui has 8 pencils. Her aunt in Kpando gives her some more. Now she has 14. Use stones to find how many her aunt gave. 8 + __ = 14.
Lamley had 16 toffees. She shared some with friends in Nungua. She has 9 left. How many did she share? 16 - __ = 9.
Musah has 11 goats in Yendi. Issah has 15 goats. Draw the goats and match them. How many more goats does Issah have?

math:B1.1.2.2.2.text: Yaa has 12 plantains in Obuasi. She fries 9 for kelewele. To find what is left, think 9 + __ = 12. So what is 12 - 9?
A canoe at Elmina has seats for 15 fishermen. 11 are in. Think 11 + __ = 15. So what is 15 - 11?
Mariama knows that 7 + 6 = 13. She has 13 shea nuts in Savelugu and gives away 6. Use her fact to find 13 - 6.

math:B1.1.2.2.3.text: Make up a story for 8 + 5 = __. Use mangoes at a market in Techiman. Then find the answer.
Tell a story about girls playing ampe in Dambai that fits 14 - 6 = __. What is the answer?
Kwabena wrote 9 + __ = 12. Tell a story about a trotro and its riders that fits his sum. Find the missing number.

math:B1.1.2.3.1.text: Korkor has 4 oranges in each hand at Somanya market. Double 4. How many oranges does she have?
Kuukua wants 10 bottle tops for a game in Swedru. She has 7. How many more does she need to make 10?
Kwesi in Axim has 6 marbles. Say the number that is 2 more. Say the number that is 1 less. Do it fast, with no counters.

math:B1.1.2.4.1.text: Dzifa has 8 fish at Keta beach. Her brother brings 5 more. Start at 8 and count on 5. How many fish are there now?
There are 17 yams in a barn in Kintampo. Nana takes out 4. Start at 17 and count back 4. How many yams are left?
Odoi buys 6 pens, 3 rulers and 4 erasers in Madina. Add 6 and 4 first to make 10. Then add 3. How many things did he buy?

math:B1.1.2.4.2.text: Afua picked 11 tomatoes on a farm near Wenchi. Her father picked 7. How many tomatoes did they pick in all?
Tiyumba had 19 pieces of kulikuli to sell in Tamale. By noon 12 were sold. How many were left?
Ekow caught 9 crabs at Winneba. Araba caught 14. How many more crabs did Araba catch than Ekow?

math:B1.1.3.1.1.text: A mother in Cape Coast cuts one orange into 2 equal parts for Kobina and Esi. What do we call each part? Draw it.
Nyameke breaks a stick of sugarcane in Axim into two pieces. One piece is long and one is short. Did he make halves? Say why.
Fold a sheet of paper so that the two parts match, as Adongo did in Navrongo. Shade one part. What part of the paper is shaded?

math:B1.1.3.1.2.text: Auntie Akua cuts 3 oranges in half at her stall in Nsawam. Count the pieces: one half, two halves, and so on. How many halves are there?
Fati has 4 half slices of boiled yam on a plate in Salaga. Count them aloud in halves. How many whole slices do they make?
Draw 5 half balls of kenkey, like the ones Tsotsoo shares in Accra. Count them: one half, two halves, and so on. What do you say last?

math:B1.1.4.1.1.text: Kwaku in Goaso has one 50 pesewas coin. His sister has only 10 pesewas coins. How many of her coins are worth the same as his one coin?
Hawa saves coins in a tin in Damongo. She has two 50 pesewas coins. Which one coin has the same value as these two?
Mawusi sorts coins at her mother's shop in Ho. Put them in order from least value to most: 20 pesewas, 5 pesewas, GH₵ 1, 50 pesewas, 10 pesewas.

math:B1.2.1.1.1.text: A kente strip from Bonwire goes yellow, green, red, yellow, green, red. Which three colours come next?
In a clapping game in Jasikan, girls go clap, clap, jump, clap, clap, jump. Do the pattern. What comes after the next two claps?
Suglo lines up seeds in Tolon: maize, bean, bean, maize, bean, maize, bean, bean. One seed is missing. Where does it go? What is the pattern?

math:B1.3.1.1.1.text: Frimpomaa draws a big red triangle and a small blue triangle at school in Bechem. What is the same about them? Does colour or size change the name of the shape?
Look down on a water drum and a cooking pot, like the ones at Asibi's house in Bolgatanga. Which flat shape can you see at the top of each?
Cut a paper square from corner to corner, as Ofoli did in Tema. Join the two triangles to make the square again. Now put two squares side by side. What new shape is it?

math:B1.3.1.1.2.text: At a kiosk in Kasoa there is a football, a milk tin, a matchbox and a sugar cube. Which one is a sphere? Which is a cylinder? Which is a cube?
Zenabu sorts things in her mother's store in Yendi: tins of tomato, boxes of soap, an orange and a ball. Put the ones that can roll in one group. What is your rule?
Elikem has a chalk box and a tin of milk in Sogakope. Tell one way they are different. How many flat faces has the chalk box?

math:B1.3.1.1.3.text: Look at the Ghana flag. What shape is the whole flag? How many sides does it have? How many corners?
Asantewaa cuts paper shapes in Berekum: 3 circles, 2 triangles and 4 squares. Sort them by number of sides. Which group has no straight sides?
A window at Lartey's school in Aburi is a square. The door is a long rectangle. Tell one thing that is the same about the two shapes and one thing that is different.

math:B1.3.2.1.1.text: In a class in Wa, Bayuo sits in front of Amina. Mumuni sits on Amina's left. Who is behind Bayuo? Who is on Mumuni's right?
Draw a table. Put a bowl of banku on the table and a stool under it. Draw a lamp above the table. Tell a friend where each thing is.
At the lorry park in Dormaa, a taxi is between two trotros. An okada is to the right of the last trotro. Draw the row. What is next to the okada?

math:B1.3.3.1.1.text: Stand a pencil and a piece of chalk on your desk, as Yayra does in Hohoe. Which is taller? Which is shorter?
Hold a yam in one hand and an orange in the other, like Donkor at Atebubu market. Which is heavier? Which is lighter?
Asana has a long piece of cloth. Rukaya has a short one. They lay them side by side in Gambaga. How can they tell which is longer?

math:B1.4.1.1.1.text: In Ato's class in Breman Asikuma, 6 pupils like kenkey, 4 like banku and 5 like rice. Draw one small picture for each pupil in three rows.
Naa counts at the gate in Madina: 5 taxis, 7 trotros and 3 okadas. Use bottle tops to show each group in its own line. How many are there altogether?
Stand boys in one line and girls in another, as they do at assembly in Tumu. Put down one stone for each child. Which line has more stones?

math:B1.4.1.1.2.text: A class in Sefwi Wiawso picks a best fruit. Mango gets 8 votes, orange 5 and banana 7. How many pupils voted? How many more chose mango than orange?
Awuni keeps animals in Zebilla: 9 goats, 6 sheep and 4 guinea fowl. Make a tally chart. Which group is smallest? How many animals in all?
A picture chart shows how pupils in Anloga get to school: 10 walk, 3 ride a bicycle and 2 take a trotro. How many pupils is that? How many fewer ride than walk?

math:B2.1.1.1.1.text: A cocoa farmer in Enchi puts pods in heaps of 10. He has 34 heaps. Count in tens. How many pods is that?
Oranges at Agona Nkwanta market sell in piles of 5. Count in fives from 100: 100, 105, 110. What are the next four numbers?
Sumaila counts back in tens as he packs yams in Kintampo: 500, 490, 480, 460, 450. He skipped one number. Which one?

math:B2.1.1.1.2.text: A chart shows 301 to 400 with ten numbers in a row. Find 345, the number of Kwabena's house in Kenyasi. Which number is before it? After it? Just below it?
Dede has a 1 to 100 chart in Somanya. She points to 67. Name the numbers above it, below it, on its left and on its right.
A chart in Rashida's class in Damongo shows 501 to 600 in rows of ten. Which number is just above 580? Which number is just below 529?

math:B2.1.1.1.3.text: Akolgo in Sirigu cuts a stick as long as 10 hand-spans. He lays it along the classroom 6 times, then 4 more hand-spans. How many hand-spans long is the room?
Esi fills a big drum in Mankessim. Each bucket holds 10 cups. She pours in 12 buckets and 5 cups. How many cups of water are in the drum?
Count your strides from the classroom door to the school gate, as Senyo does in Aflao. Group them in tens and ones. How many strides is it?

math:B2.1.1.1.4.text: Ama ties broomsticks in bundles of 10 in Konongo. She has 5 bundles and 8 loose sticks. How many sticks is that? Which digit shows the tens?
A waakye seller in Madina has 63 leaves for wrapping. How many tens and how many ones are in 63? Write 63 as a sum in two ways.
Mbo says the 3 in 37 and the 3 in 73 mean the same. His friend in Savelugu says no. Who is right? Tell what each 3 stands for.

math:B2.1.1.1.5.text: A school in Bibiani has 298 pupils. Is 298 closer to 300 or to 200? How many less than 300 is it? Tell one more thing about 298.
Kwesi has 24 oranges at Swedru market. Show two ways to put them in equal piles. Say how many piles and how many in each pile.
One lorry carries 450 tubers of yam from Salaga. Another carries 45. Is 450 a little more or a lot more than 45? Write 450 as hundreds and tens.

math:B2.1.1.1.6.text: Abugri has 38 guinea fowl in Zebilla. Awuni has 83. Who has more? Look at the tens. Write the two numbers with > or < between them.
Four ampe teams in Apam score 56, 65, 49 and 60. Put the scores in order from smallest to biggest.
A number line in Delali's book in Kpando shows 70, 71, __, 73, __, 75. Fill in the gaps. How do you know?

math:B2.1.2.1.1.text: Kwadwo picks 26 mangoes and Serwaa picks 43 in Ejura. Add 26 + 43. Then add 43 + 26. What do you notice?
A trotro in Tarkwa has 31 people in it. At the next stop 0 people get on. How many are in it now? What does adding 0 do to a number?
Atampoka had 45 baskets in Bolgatanga. She wove some more and now has 58. Which sum fits: 45 + __ = 58 or 58 + 45 = __? Find the missing number.

math:B2.1.2.2.1.text: Nii has 20 + 15 crabs at Chorkor. Ayeley has 40 - 5 crabs. Are the two amounts equal? Write = or ≠ between 20 + 15 and 40 - 5.
Yaw counts cocoa bags in Goaso. He says 36 + 20 is the same as 60. Is he right? Write 36 + 20 __ 60 with = or ≠.
Fuseina had 50 shea nuts in Tolon and used 32. To find 50 - 32, think 32 + __ = 50. What is the missing number?

math:B2.1.2.3.1.text: One crate in Koforidua has 8 bottles of sobolo. Another has 9. Think double 8 and 1 more. How many bottles are there?
Kuukua has 7 fish at Moree and Ebo brings 6. Make 10 first: 7 + 3. Then add the 3 that are left. How many fish?
Alhassan has 15 kola nuts in Kumbungu. He gives 6 away. Think 6 + __ = 15. How many does he keep?

math:B2.1.2.4.1.text: Awo bakes 37 loaves in the morning and 45 in the afternoon in Nsawam. Write the sum in tens and ones columns. How many loaves did she bake?
A lorry park in Atebubu has 64 cars. 28 drive away. Set it out in tens and ones and subtract. How many cars stay?
Edem has 52 exercise books in his shop in Ho. He sells 21. Subtract the ones, then the tens. How many books are left?

math:B2.1.2.4.2.text: Afua sells 38 oranges on Monday and 27 on Tuesday at Kejetia Market. Add the tens: 30 + 20. Add the ones: 8 + 7. What is the total?
Wumpini has 46 yams in Tamale and gets 33 more. Start at 46. Jump on 10 three times. Then add 3. How many yams has he now?
Senyo has GH₵ 49. His aunt in Anloga gives him GH₵ 25. Move GH₵ 1 from the 25 to the 49. Now add 50 + 24. How much has he?

math:B2.1.2.4.3.text: Yaa has 42 tomatoes at Agbogbloshie market. She sells 15 before noon and 12 after noon. How many are left?
Ibrahim had GH₵ 60. He paid GH₵ 8 for a trotro in Sawla and GH₵ 20 for waakye. How much money is left?
Class 2 in Jirapa has 28 girls and 25 boys. 6 pupils are away today. How many pupils are in class?

math:B2.1.3.1.1.text: A mother in Kibi cuts a round loaf of bread into 4 equal parts for four children. What do we call each part? Draw the loaf and shade one part.
Opoku and Akosua share one ball of banku equally in Mampong. Four friends share another ball of the same size equally. Who gets a bigger piece, Opoku or one of the four?
Tetteh folds a paper kite twice in Ada so that it has 4 equal parts. He colours 1 part. What part is coloured: a half or a quarter?

math:B2.1.3.1.2.text: Ayisha cuts 2 watermelons into quarters in Walewale. Count them: one quarter, two quarters, and so on. How many quarters are there?
A seller in Dodowa has 5 half pawpaws on her table. Count them in halves: one half, two halves, and so on. What do you say last?
Ofori has 3 quarter pieces of sugarcane in Akim Oda. Pokuaa brings 2 more quarter pieces. Count them all in quarters. What do you say last?

math:B2.1.3.1.3.text: Enyonam cuts one orange into halves in Kpando. Kosi cuts one orange into quarters. How many pieces does each child have?
How many quarter slices of yam make one half slice? Azure in Tongo puts two quarters next to a half to check. What does he see?
A flat loaf of bread in Offinso is cut into 4 equal parts. How many parts make the whole loaf? How many parts make half the loaf?

math:B2.1.4.1.1.text: Nyarko takes one GH₵ 20 note, one GH₵ 10 note and two GH₵ 5 notes to the market in Sunyani. How much money has she?
Kweku in Tarkwa wants to change one GH₵ 10 note. How many GH₵ 2 notes have the same value?
Salifu in Wa has a GH₵ 5 note, three GH₵ 2 coins and two 50 pesewas coins. How much is that altogether?

math:B2.2.1.1.1.text: Adjeley in Teshie has GH₵ 15. She saves GH₵ 5 more each week: 15, 20, 25, 30. What is the rule? What are the next three numbers?
Bags of maize leave a store in Ejura. First 90 are left, then 80, 70, 60. What is the rule? How many are left after the next two trips?
Dery writes the house numbers on his side of a street in Nandom: 12, 14, 16, 19, 20. One is wrong. Which one? What should it be?

math:B2.2.1.1.2.text: Araba sets out bofrot in rows of 3 in Dunkwa. One row has 3, two rows have 6, three rows have 9. How many in four rows? In five rows? What is the rule?
Make your own number pattern with the rule 'take away 2'. Start at 30, the number of oranges on Akwasi's table in Bekwai. Write six numbers.
Rahinatu threads beads in Bole. Each string has 4 more beads than the last: 4, 8, 12, 16. Write the next two numbers. Say the rule.

math:B2.3.1.1.1.text: Lartey finds a milk tin, a water drum and a roll of cloth in Aburi. What is the same about their shapes? What do we call this solid?
Kafui in Peki sorts a football, an orange, a sugar cube, a ludo dice and a chalk box. One group has flat faces. One has none. Which group gets the orange?
The roof of a round hut in Sirigu comes to a point at the top. Which solid does the roof look like: a cube, a cone or a sphere? How many corners has a cube?

math:B2.3.1.1.2.text: Walk around your school like Adwoa's class in Bechem. Find a rectangle, a circle and a triangle. Say where you saw each one.
Mawuli draws a shape with 5 sides and 5 corners in Hohoe. Selasi draws one with 6 sides and 6 corners. Name each shape.
Sort these by number of corners: the Ghana flag, a square floor tile, a road sign with 3 sides and a round coin. Which ones have 4 corners?

math:B2.3.1.1.3.text: Use sticks, like Akanbang in Sandema, to make a shape with 3 sides. Then make one with 4 equal sides and square corners. Name the two shapes.
Draw a shape with 4 sides and 4 corners where two sides are longer, like a door in Afriyie's house in Obuasi. What is it called?
Kojo in Saltpond traces round the bottom of a milk tin. Which shape does he get? Then he traces one face of a matchbox. Which shape is that?

math:B2.3.2.1.1.text: Take two sticks of the same length, like Nyameke in Half Assini. Lay one flat and stand one up. Does one look longer? Put them side by side to check.
Zenabu lays her ruler across her desk in Zabzugu, then along it, then slanting. Is the ruler longer any of these times? How can she show it?
Two pencils of the same length lie on Efua's desk in Elmina. One points to the door and one to the window. Efua says the first is longer. How can you check?

math:B2.3.3.1.1.text: Would you use bottle tops or pencil lengths to measure the blackboard at your school in Kadjebi? Say why. Then guess the number and measure.
Kwaku measures a desk in Nkoranza with matchsticks and gets 24. Afia uses pencils and gets 6. Why did Kwaku get a bigger number for the same desk?
A gari seller in Kasoa uses a big tin called an olonka. Guess how many small cups of gari fill a big tin. Then count to check with your own cup and tin.

math:B2.3.3.1.2.text: Line up a tuber of yam, a stick of cassava and a finger of plantain, as at Techiman market. Which is longest? Which is shortest? Put them in order.
Fati, Suglo and Napari stand back to back in Karaga. Fati is taller than Suglo. Napari is taller than Fati. Who is tallest? Who is shortest?
Lift a pawpaw, a mango and a coconut one by one, like Ekow in Sekondi. Which feels heaviest? Which is lightest? Put them in order.

math:B2.3.3.2.1.text: A teacher and little Abena both measure the same door in Akim Oda with hand-spans. He gets 9. She gets 14. Why are the numbers not the same?
A tailor in Kumasi is asked for cloth 'as long as 6 hand-spans'. Whose hand should he use? What could everyone use so that the length is always the same?
Three pupils in Lawra measure the school veranda with their own strides. They get 18, 21 and 16. Why do they differ? What tool would give them all the same answer?

math:B2.3.3.3.1.text: Ghana's Independence Day is 6 March. Find it on this year's calendar. What day of the week is it? Which month comes just before March?
Sena's grandmother comes to stay in Keta for one week and 3 days. How many days is that?
Serwaa in Mampong has her birthday in the tenth month. Which month is that? How many months come after it before the year ends?

math:B2.3.3.3.2.text: Count slow claps while a friend skips round the school flag pole twice, as pupils do in Juaboso. How many claps did it take?
Which of these takes more than an hour? Peeling an orange. Singing a song. A bus trip from Accra to Kumasi.
School in Kintampo starts at 8 o'clock and closes at 2 o'clock. Count the hours on the clock. How long are pupils in school?

math:B2.4.1.1.1.text: Ask ten classmates: do you like jollof, waakye or banku best? Make a tally mark for each answer. Which food wins?
Adongo stands by the road in Navrongo. For ten minutes he makes a tally of bicycles, okadas and cars. Write one question his tally chart can answer.
A tally chart in Worawora shows the games pupils like: ampe 8, football 11, oware 4. Which game is liked least? How many pupils were asked?

math:B2.4.1.2.1.text: In a picture graph, one fish stands for 2 baskets. Elmina has 4 fish pictures, Axim has 3 and Keta has 5. How many baskets did Keta land? How many in all?
Pupils in Damongo vote for a fruit: 6 mango, 4 orange, 2 pawpaw. Draw a picture graph. Let one picture stand for 2 pupils. How many pictures for mango?
Lamley makes a graph with bottle tops in Nungua: 7 for pupils who like ampe, 5 for football and 3 for oware. How many more like ampe than oware?

math:B3.1.1.1.1.text: A cocoa depot in Sefwi Wiawso stacks bags in hundreds. Count on in hundreds from 2,700: 2,700, 2,800. Write the next four numbers.
Kwadwo in Obuasi counts in fifties: 450, 500, 550, 650. He missed one number. Which one? What comes after 650?
About how many people fit in a full trotro: 2, 20 or 200? About how many pupils are in a big school in Tema: 8, 80 or 800? Say why.

math:B3.1.1.1.2.text: A chart in a classroom in Prestea shows 2,301 to 2,400 in rows of ten. Find 2,345. Which number is on its left? On its right? Just above? Just below?
Dzifa's chart in Kpeve counts in hundreds with ten numbers in a row: 100, 200, and on up to 10,000. Which number is right after 4,900? Which is just under 4,900?
On a 1 to 100 chart, Sulemana in Saboba starts at 34. He moves down two rows and one step to the right. Where does he land?

math:B3.1.1.1.3.text: Traders at Techiman market sold 3,472 tubers of yam. What does the 4 stand for? Write 3,472 as thousands + hundreds + tens + ones.
A school in Dambai has 635 pupils. Read the number aloud the right way. How many hundreds, tens and ones does it have?
Korkor makes beads in Odumase Krobo. She made 5,050 one year and 5,500 the next. What is the value of each 5 in 5,050? Which number is bigger?

math:B3.1.1.1.4.text: Traders in Nkawkaw sold 4,580 oranges. Traders in Agona Swedru sold 4,850. Which town sold more? Which digit tells you? Write the numbers with > or <.
Three schools in Bolgatanga have 1,209, 989 and 1,290 pupils. Put the numbers in order from least to most.
Yaw in Bekwai reads a number line: 6,000, 6,100, __, 6,300, 6,500. Fill the gap. Which number was left out near the end?

math:B3.1.1.2.1.text: Agyei walks 5 steps forward from the flag pole at his school in Goaso. Mansa walks 5 steps backward. How are their moves the same? How are they opposite?
A trotro goes north from Kumasi to Techiman. What is the opposite trip? Now give the opposite of each word: up, gain, forward, left.
Oforiwaa in Suhum saves GH₵ 3 on Monday and spends GH₵ 3 on Tuesday. Why are these opposite? What has happened to her money after the two days?

math:B3.1.1.2.2.text: A canoe floats on the sea at Dixcove. A bird flies 6 metres above the water. A fish swims 4 metres below. Write each one with a + or - sign.
The ground beside a well in Gushegu is 0. The top of the wall is 1 metre up. The water is 7 metres down. Write both as + or - numbers.
Mount Afadja near Hohoe rises 885 metres above sea level. Is that a + or a - number? What kind of place would have a - number?

math:B3.1.1.3.1.text: Draw a number line from -10 to 10 on the ground, like pupils in Jasikan. Stand on 0. Kafui takes 3 steps to the right. Yao takes 3 steps to the left. Name each number.
Azara in Salaga owes her friend GH₵ 5. Fuseini has GH₵ 5 saved. Which number shows each one: 5 or -5? Mark both on a number line.
Ebo in Anomabo says -8 is to the left of 0 on the number line. Is he right? Which is further from 0: -8 or 6?

math:B3.1.1.3.2.text: Chalk a number line from -10 to 10 at school in Lawra. Start on 3 and hop back 5. Say each number as you hop. Where do you land?
Count on from -4 to 4 and say every number. Mawuli in Kpando says that is 8 hops. Check by counting the hops.
Adwoa stands on -6 on a floor number line in Konongo. She hops forward 9. Does she pass zero? Where does she stop?

math:B3.1.2.1.1.text: A school in Nadowli has 346 girls and 289 boys. Add in columns, starting with the ones. How many pupils are there?
A trader at Makola Market had 702 yards of cloth and sold 458. Subtract in columns. How many yards are left?
Fishers at Yeji landed 318 baskets of fish on Friday and some more on Saturday. That made 704 in all. Solve 318 + ☐ = 704. What does the box stand for?

math:B3.1.2.2.1.text: One lorry carries 250 + 150 bags of maize from Ejura. Another carries 500 - 100 bags. Write = or ≠ between the two sums.
Naa adds the pupils of two schools in Tema. She says 300 + 240 is equal to 520. Is she right? Write 300 + 240 __ 520 with = or ≠.
A farmer in Bechem has 400 cocoa pods and breaks 280. To find 400 - 280, think 280 + __ = 400. What is the missing number?

math:B3.1.2.3.1.text: Ekua sold 45 balls of kenkey in the morning and 46 at night in Mankessim. Think double 45 and 1 more. How many did she sell?
A taxi driver in Sunyani drove 38 km before lunch and 47 km after. Move 2 from the 47 to the 38, then add. How far did he drive?
Issah has 72 guinea fowl in Walewale and sells 29. Take away 30, then add 1 back. How many are left?

math:B3.1.2.4.1.text: A kente weaver in Bonwire sold 245 strips last year and 332 this year. Add the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones. What is the total?
Two schools in Nkwanta have 158 and 264 pupils. Show 158 + 264 with bundles of 100, 10 and 1 sticks. Swap 10 ones for a ten when you can. What is the sum?
Hawa has 407 shea nuts in Damongo and picks 95 more. Draw hundreds, tens and ones to add them. How many nuts has she now?

math:B3.1.2.4.2.text: A store in Koforidua had some bags of rice. It sold 150 and has 275 left. Solve ☐ - 150 = 275. How many bags were there at first?
Kwesi's school in Takoradi needs 600 chairs and has 395. Count up from 395: 5 more makes 400, then 200 more. How many chairs are missing?
A farmer near Kete Krachi had 635 yams and sold 198. Take away 200, then add 2 back. How many yams are left?

math:B3.1.2.4.3.text: A trotro station in Madina had 412 riders in the morning and 379 in the evening. Round each number to the nearest hundred. About how many riders in all?
A school in Berekum has 680 pupils. 310 are boys. About how many are girls? Use 700 and 300 to estimate. Then find the exact answer. Was your estimate close?
Efua needs about 900 oranges for a festival in Cape Coast. She has heaps of 520 and 290. Estimate the total. Does she have enough?

math:B3.1.2.4.4.text: A farm in Kenyasi packs 325 pawpaws, then 164 more. The next day it packs 164, then 325. Work out both totals. What do you notice?
Habiba counts books in Jirapa. She says 408 + 91 is the same as 91 + 408 without working it out. Is she right? Why? Now find the sum.
Amina in Bimbilla knows that 517 + 260 = 777. What is 260 + 517? Does the order matter for take away too? Try 9 - 4 and 4 - 9.

math:B3.1.2.5.1.text: Auntie Akweley puts kelewele in 4 bags with 5 pieces in each at her stall in Osu. Draw the bags. Write a multiplication sentence. How many pieces?
Abdulai in Savelugu has 15 shea nuts. He makes 3 equal groups. How many in each? Write it with ×. Now make 5 equal groups and write that too.
3 okadas wait at a junction in Sandema. Each has 2 wheels. Skip count in twos to find the number of wheels. Write the multiplication sentence.

math:B3.1.2.5.2.text: Oranges sit in 4 rows of 5 on a table at Asesewa market. Draw dots for them. Write the multiplication sentence and the total.
Lay 3 sticks down and 4 sticks across them, as Delali did in Aflao. Count the points where the sticks cross. Which multiplication sentence does this show?
Desks in a classroom in Tumu stand in 5 rows with 3 in each row. Draw them. Turn your drawing sideways. Is 5 × 3 the same as 3 × 5? How many desks?

math:B3.1.2.6.1.text: Four friends in Kpetoe share 20 mangoes equally. Give out one mango at a time until none are left. How many does each friend get?
Nana shares 15 pieces of yam equally on 3 plates in Atebubu. Draw the plates. How many pieces go on each plate?
Yakubu has 18 guinea fowl eggs in Nalerigu. He packs them equally into 2 baskets. How many eggs are in each? Write the division sentence.

math:B3.1.2.6.2.text: Araba has 16 fish at Shama. She puts 4 on each tray. Keep taking away 4 until none are left. How many trays does she fill?
A taxi in Berekum takes 4 riders at a time. 20 people wait. Take away 4 for each trip. How many trips carry them all?
Wumpini ties 15 maize cobs in bunches of 5 in Tolon. Show it as 15 - 5 - 5 - 5. How many bunches does he make?

math:B3.1.2.6.3.text: 20 pupils in Dormaa sit 5 to a bench. Think: what times 5 makes 20? So what is 20 ÷ 5?
Selorm knows that 3 × 6 = 18. He has 18 oranges in Keta to put in 3 equal bags. Use his fact to find 18 ÷ 3.
Fill the gaps for Adjoa in Swedru: __ × 2 = 16, so 16 ÷ 2 = __. Tell a short story about 16 sticks of chalk that fits.

math:B3.1.3.1.1.text: A baker in Kumasi cuts a loaf into 5 equal slices. Osei eats one slice. What fraction of the loaf did he eat? Write it in words and in numbers.
A farmer in Asankragwa splits his field into 8 equal plots. He plants cassava on 3 of them. Write the fraction that has cassava. What does the 8 tell you?
Draw a strip of kente cloth with 4 equal parts. Colour 1 part gold. What fraction is gold? What fraction is not gold?

math:B3.1.3.1.2.text: There are 12 girls in Naa's ampe group in La. Half of them wear red. How many is that? One quarter wear white. How many is that?
Draw a line from 0 to 1 for the road from Senyo's house to his school in Akatsi. Split it into 4 equal parts. Mark where he is after 3/4 of the way.
Azure has 10 goats in Paga. 3 of them are brown. What fraction of the goats is brown? Write it in words and in numbers.

math:B3.1.3.1.3.text: Two balls of banku of the same size are shared in Ho. Sena gets 1/2 of one. Edem gets 1/4 of the other. Who gets more? Draw to show why.
Friends in Wenchi cut a sugarcane stick into 8 equal bits. Yaw gets 3/8, Afia 1/8 and Takyi 4/8. Put the fractions in order from smallest to largest.
Which is bigger: 1/3 of a yam or 1/5 of the same yam? Bayor in Nandom says 1/5, because 5 is more than 3. Is he right? Say why.

math:B3.1.4.1.1.text: Zakari buys waakye for GH₵ 15 at a stall in Nima. He pays with a GH₵ 20 note. How much change does he get? Which notes or coins could it be?
Ewurama buys 3 exercise books at GH₵ 6 each in Winneba. She pays with a GH₵ 50 note. How much change should she get?
Memuna pays GH₵ 25 for groundnuts at Tamale market. Show three different ways to make GH₵ 25 with GH₵ 5, GH₵ 10 and GH₵ 20 notes.

math:B3.2.1.1.1.text: A mason in Duayaw Nkwanta lays 4 more blocks in each row: 4, 8, 12, 16. What is the rule? Write the next three numbers.
A water tank in Bole holds 60 buckets. Each day 6 buckets are used: 60, 54, 48, 42. Say the rule. How many are left after the next two days?
Achiaa in Kumasi writes down her susu savings: 10, 20, 30, 50, 60. One number is missing. Which one? Then make your own pattern with the rule 'take away 5'.

math:B3.3.1.1.1.text: Pick up a matchbox, like Kwabena in Ejisu. How many faces has it? How many edges? How many corners? What shape is each face?
A tin of milk and a sugar cube sit on Fati's table in Salaga. Which one has a curved face? Which has 8 corners? Which has 12 edges?
Sort these by number of sides: a road sign with 3 sides, a square tile, the Ghana flag and a five-sided kite. Which two belong together?

math:B3.3.1.1.2.text: Open a pair of scissors a little, then wide, like a tailor at Kejetia Market. Which way makes the bigger angle? Draw both angles.
Look at the black star on the Ghana flag. How many sharp points does it have? Draw one point with two straight lines. What do we call the turn between the lines?
Draw a triangle and a four-sided shape with a ruler, like Nii at school in Teshie. Mark every angle with a small curve. How many angles are in each shape?

math:B3.3.1.1.3.text: Fold a sheet of paper twice to make a square corner. Test the corners of your exercise book and your desk, like Asabea in Nkawkaw. Which are right angles?
Hold your paper square corner against the hands of a clock at 3 o'clock, then at 1 o'clock. Atanga in Bongo says only one is a right angle. Which one?
Find three things at your school in Kpandai with square corners and one thing whose corner is not square. Check each one with your paper corner.

math:B3.3.1.1.4.text: Ashitey flies a kite at Labadi beach. It has 4 sides but is not a square or a rectangle. Draw a four-sided shape like that. What do all four-sided shapes share?
Enyonam cuts out a rectangle, a square and a rhombus in Sogakope. Which have 4 equal sides? Which have 4 square corners? Which one has both?
Draw a shape with 4 sides where only one pair of sides runs side by side and never meets, like the side of a wheelbarrow in Prang. Name the shape.

math:B3.3.2.1.1.text: A stick lies on a number line from 3 to 8 in Yaa's book in Mampong. Count the unit jumps. How long is the stick?
Lay a pencil from 0 to 6 on a number line. Slide it so that it starts at 4. Where does it end? Abu in Buipe says its length did not change. Why is he right?
On a number line of a road in Assin Fosu, the school is at 2 and the market is at 9. How many units apart are they?

math:B3.3.3.1.1.text: A tailor in Koforidua has a tape 1 metre long. How many centimetres is that? How many are in 3 metres?
Would you use centimetres or metres to measure a pencil? A football field in Obuasi? The height of a door? Say why each time.
Ebo's desk in Twifo Praso is 120 cm long. Is that more or less than 1 metre? By how many centimetres?

math:B3.3.3.1.2.text: Pupils in Bibiani chose a little finger nail for about 1 cm and one big stride for about 1 m. Find your own thing for 1 cm and for 1 m. Say why you chose them.
Sena in Dzodze uses the width of her finger for 1 cm. About how many finger widths long is your pencil? Check with a ruler.
Yakubu says a door at his school in Gambaga is about 2 big strides tall. Is his stride close to 1 cm or to 1 m? About how tall is the door?

math:B3.3.3.1.3.text: A school garden in Dormaa is a rectangle 8 m long and 5 m wide. How much fence goes all the way round it?
Guess the distance round your exercise book in centimetres. Then measure each side with a ruler and add, like Afi in Kpando. How close was your guess?
Draw two different shapes that each have a distance round of 12 cm, like floor tiles at a shop in Tema. Use a ruler or squared paper.

math:B3.3.3.2.1.text: A bag of rice in a Takoradi shop is 1 kilogram. How many grams is that? How many grams are in half a kilogram?
A sachet of water holds 500 ml. How many sachets make 1 litre? Konadu in Agogo drinks 3 sachets a day. Is that more than 1 litre?
Would you use grams or kilograms to weigh a bag of maize in Funsi? One egg? Would you use litres or millilitres for a bucket of water? A spoon of oil?

math:B3.3.3.2.2.text: Hold a 1 kg bag of sugar. Then hold a tuber of yam, like Napari in Yendi. Is the yam more or less than 1 kg? Check on a scale.
A sachet of water is half a litre. Guess how many sachets fill a small bucket. Kwesi in Komenda guessed 20. Pour and count to check your guess.
Guess the order from lightest to heaviest: a mango, a 1 kg bag of gari and a school bag full of books. Then weigh them, as pupils did in Drobo.

math:B3.3.3.3.1.text: An oware game in Ada starts at 10.15 a.m. and ends at 10.40 a.m. How long did the game last?
A bus leaves Accra at 7.00 a.m. and gets to Cape Coast at 9.30 a.m. How long is the trip?
Which of these takes about 10 minutes: eating a bowl of koko, growing maize, or walking from Tamale to Accra? Name something that takes months.

math:B3.3.3.3.2.text: Ghana's Independence Day is 6 March and Republic Day is 1 July. Which comes first in the year? Which whole months lie between March and July?
The school holiday in Sekondi runs from 13 April to 3 May, counting both days. Use a calendar. How many days is that? How many weeks?
Farmers' Day in Ghana is the first Friday of December. Find it on this year's calendar. What is the date? What day of the week is 25 December?

math:B3.3.3.3.3.text: Kofi in Suhum helps to boil eggs for 3 minutes. How many seconds is that?
The trotro from Kasoa to Winneba takes 1 hour. Aba has been riding for 40 minutes. How many minutes are left?
Memuna's mother in Wa sells koko every day in June. On how many days does she sell? How many days would it be in July?

math:B3.4.1.1.1.text: Ask 20 schoolmates how they come to school: walk, bicycle, trotro or okada. Record with tally marks in a table. Which way is most common?
Lariba counts birds on her farm in Garu: Monday 12, Tuesday 9, Wednesday 15. Put these in a table. On which day did she see the most? How many in all?
What question could you answer by counting what sellers bring to a market like the one in Kpassa, such as yam, plantain and cassava? Plan a tally chart for it.

math:B3.4.1.2.1.text: A graph shows bags of cocoa from three farms near Juaboso. One picture means 5 bags. Farm A has 4 pictures, B has 6 and C has 3. How many bags from B? How many in all?
Draw a picture graph of fish sold in Axim: Monday 20, Tuesday 30, Wednesday 10. Let one fish picture mean 10 fish. Add a title and a key.
A bar graph shows favourite foods in a class in Gwollu: tuo zaafi 12, jollof 16, waakye 8. How many more chose jollof than waakye? How many pupils voted?

math:B4.1.1.1.1.text: A nursery in Goaso packs cocoa seedlings in crates of 10,000, boxes of 1,000 and trays of 100. Which crates, boxes and trays make exactly 32,400 seedlings?
Abukari sold yams in Tamale for GH₵ 3,650. Show this amount with play GH₵ 100, GH₵ 10 and GH₵ 1 notes, using as few notes as you can. How many of each note do you need?
On graph paper, let one small square stand for 100 bags of maize. A store in Techiman holds 14,200 bags. How many small squares must you shade to show this number?

math:B4.1.1.1.2.text: The gate at Baba Yara Stadium in Kumasi counted 38,407 fans. Write this number in words. Then write it in expanded form.
A radio presenter in Wa says, 'Sixty-two thousand and fifty-nine people sent in votes.' Write this number in figures.
A water factory in Cape Coast filled 70,315 sachets today. Read the number aloud and write it in words. What is the value of the digit 7?

math:B4.1.1.1.3.text: Seats at a durbar ground in Kumasi are numbered in 500s: 20,000, 20,500, 21,000 and so on. Which numbers come just before and just after 23,500?
A chart at a cocoa shed in Sefwi Wiawso counts in 500s with six numbers in each row. Row one starts at 40,000 and row two starts at 43,000. Which number sits right below 41,500?
Efua in Winneba hides one number on a chart that goes up in 500s. The number before it is 67,500 and the number after it is 68,500. What is the hidden number?

math:B4.1.1.1.4.text: Traders at Bolgatanga market sold 8,645 baskets in March and 8,654 in April. Write the two numbers with <, = or > between them. Which month had more sales?
Four canoes at Elmina landed 2,873, 2,378, 2,783 and 2,738 fish. Put the four catches in order from smallest to largest.
Dery planted 9,120 onion seedlings near Lawra and Ziem planted 9,102. Put <, = or > between the two numbers. Who planted more, and by how many?

math:B4.1.1.1.5.text: A lorry carried 6,748 tubers of yam from Yendi to Accra. Round this number to the nearest ten, the nearest hundred and the nearest thousand.
Akosua sold 4,365 oranges at Nkawkaw. Round the number up to the next hundred. Then round it down to the hundred below. Which of the two is closer to 4,365?
A school in Hohoe bought 2,890 exercise books and 3,120 pencils. Round each number to the nearest thousand to estimate how many items it bought in all.

math:B4.1.1.1.6.text: Kwabena loads oranges onto a truck in Sunyani, 50 at a time. His tally shows 2,730. What will it show after each of the next five loads?
A shea butter group in Savelugu has 6,340 bars of soap. They send out 100 bars each day. Count back in 100s to find how many bars are left after each of the next four days.
Mawuli of Kpando counts cedis in 50s: 3,850, 3,900, 3,950, 4,050, 4,100. Which number did he leave out? Say the count correctly.

math:B4.1.1.2.1.text: The clock on a chapel in Cape Coast has Roman numerals. Which numbers do the marks IV, IX and XII stand for?
A class in Navrongo makes Roman numeral cards using only the letters I, V and X. Which letters, in which order, do they need to show 8, 14 and 26?
The chapters in Adjeley's storybook are numbered I to XXX. She is on chapter XIX. Which numeral is on the next chapter? Which is on the one before?

math:B4.1.1.2.2.text: Kojo from Elmina is 9, his sister Araba is 16 and their uncle's shop is 27 years old. Write the three numbers in Roman numerals.
Three houses on a street in Keta are marked XVII, XXI and XXVIII. Write the three house numbers in ordinary figures.
An ampe contest in Dambai has rounds numbered in Roman numerals. Count aloud and write the rounds from XVI to XXII.

math:B4.1.1.3.1.text: Enyonam has 36 mangoes to sell at Ho market. She wants equal heaps with none left over. List every heap size she can use.
A teacher in Wenchi puts 28 desks in equal rows. Write all the pairs of rows and desks in a row that work. Then list the factors of 28.
Tetteh shares 48 oware seeds equally among friends in Ada, with none left. Can he share among 5 friends? Among 6? List all the factors of 48.

math:B4.1.1.3.2.text: Afia has 18 pawpaws and 30 oranges at Techiman market. She packs all of them into baskets that each hold the same mix of fruit. What is the greatest number of baskets she can fill?
A fisherman at Axim has ropes of 24 m and 40 m. He cuts both into pieces of the same length with nothing left over. What is the longest piece he can cut?
A school in Bawku shares 16 footballs and 28 skipping ropes equally among its classes, with none left. List the common factors of 16 and 28. Which is the highest?

math:B4.1.1.3.3.text: At a station in Accra, a trotro leaves for Madina every 6 minutes and one for Kaneshie every 8 minutes. Both leave at 7:00. After how many minutes do they next leave together?
A shop in Koforidua sells exercise books in packs of 12 and pens in packs of 8. Selorm wants the same number of books and pens. What is the smallest number of each he can buy?
At a festival in Kumbungu, one drummer beats on every 9th count and another on every 12th count. On which count do they first beat together?

math:B4.1.1.3.4.text: A crate of eggs at Dormaa holds 30 eggs in 5 rows of 6. Finish the sentences: 5 and 6 are ___ of 30. 30 is a ___ of 5 and of 6.
Kafui in Aflao has 42 oranges. Without sharing them out, how can she tell if 42 is a multiple of 2? Of 3? Of 5? Give a reason each time.
Yaw from Obuasi says, 'Since 7 × 8 = 56, the number 56 is a factor of 7.' Is he right? Write two true sentences about 7, 8 and 56 using the words factor and multiple.

math:B4.1.1.3.5.text: Napari lays shea nuts in squares on the ground in Yendi: 1 nut, then 4, then 9, then 16. How many nuts make the 7th square? Explain how you know.
Add the odd numbers: 1 + 3, then 1 + 3 + 5, then 1 + 3 + 5 + 7. What kind of numbers do you get? Use this to tell Adwoa of Ejisu the sum of the first 6 odd numbers.
A tiler in Takoradi builds bigger and bigger squares of tiles: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25. Write the jumps between the numbers. What pattern do you see? How many tiles are in the next square?

math:B4.1.1.3.6.text: A square maize plot at Ejura has 9 rows with 9 plants in each row. Write the number of plants as a number multiplied by itself, and then as 9 squared.
Dede has 64 beads from Odumase Krobo. She lays them in a square with the same number in every row and column. How many beads are in each row? Write 64 as a square.
Which of these numbers of oware seeds can be laid out as a full square: 36, 48, 100, 120, 144? For each one that can, write it as a number times itself.

math:B4.1.1.4.1.text: Madam Rashida in Walewale has saved GH₵ 50 with her susu group. Her friend owes the group GH₵ 20. Write each amount as a positive or a negative number.
A kelewele seller in Osu made a profit of GH₵ 35 on Friday and a loss of GH₵ 12 on Saturday. Show each day's result with a positive or a negative number.
In a number line game at a school in Jasikan, Senyo starts at 0 and takes 6 steps to the right. Yayra starts at 0 and takes 4 steps to the left. Which numbers do they stand on?

math:B4.1.1.4.2.text: Okai from Teshie owes his brother GH₵ 5, so he writes -5. He adds GH₵ 1 every day. Count up from -5 to show his balance after each of the next 9 days.
In a number line game in Damongo, Amina stands on 7 and steps back one number at a time. Say every number she lands on until she reaches -6.
Count back in 2s from 8 to -8. Kuuire of Nandom says the number -1 is in the list. Is he right? Write the full list.

math:B4.1.2.1.1.text: A crate holds 12 bottles of sobolo. Auntie Korkor in Nungua has 7 full crates. How many bottles does she have?
Fuseini plants 9 rows of onions on his farm near Bawku, with 11 onions in each row. How many onions does he plant?
At the start of a game, each side of an oware board has 6 holes with 4 seeds in each. How many seeds are on one side? How many are on the whole board?

math:B4.1.2.2.1.text: Abena knows that 5 bunches of 8 plantains make 40 at Agogo market. How can she use this to find 6 bunches of 8 and then 7 bunches of 8 without counting again?
Coconuts cost GH₵ 8 each in Sogakope and Elikem needs 9. Work it out in your head: find the cost of 10 coconuts first, then take one away.
Zenabu in Salaga sells 2 bowls of groundnuts for GH₵ 14. Double to find the cost of 4 bowls, then double again for 8 bowls. Now halve GH₵ 14 to find the cost of 1 bowl.

math:B4.1.2.2.2.text: A cocoa farmer in Bibiani puts 300 pods into each of 6 baskets. Find the total in your head: work out 6 × 3 first, then put back the two zeros.
A box holds 5 tins of milk and a shop in Berekum has 48 boxes. Halve 48 and double 5 to find the number of tins quickly.
Kwesi buys 7 loaves of bread in Winneba at GH₵ 19 each. Find the cost in your head: think of 7 × 20, then take away 7 × 1.

math:B4.1.2.3.1.text: A school in Kintampo gives each of its 6 classes 248 exercise books. Split 248 into 200 + 40 + 8 and multiply each part by 6. How many books is that in all?
A trotro from Kasoa to Accra carries 23 people on each trip. It makes 14 trips in a week. How many people does it carry in the week?
Atanga sells 3 guinea fowls in Bolgatanga for GH₵ 135 each. How much money does he receive?

math:B4.1.2.4.1.text: Esi shares 72 pieces of kelewele equally onto 8 plates at a party in Saltpond. How many pieces go on each plate?
63 pupils in Gambaga line up in 7 equal rows for a parade. How many pupils stand in each row? Which multiplication fact helps you?
Lamptey has 54 fish to tie in bundles of 6 at Jamestown. How many bundles can he make? Can 54 also be shared into 4 equal groups? Explain.

math:B4.1.2.5.1.text: Auntie Dzifa has 96 mangoes at Kpando market. She puts the same number in each of 4 baskets. How many go in each basket?
A teacher in Goaso has 84 pencils and gives 6 to each group. Keep taking away 6s, or take away 60 first, to find how many groups get pencils.
A bakery in Nsawam shares 392 loaves of bread equally among 7 vans. Start with 7 × 50, then finish the sharing. How many loaves does each van carry?

math:B4.1.2.6.1.text: Naa Dedei buys 3 balls of kenkey at GH₵ 5 each and fish for GH₵ 12 in Osu. She pays with a GH₵ 50 note. How much change does she get?
A farmer in Asesewa picks 8 baskets of 45 tomatoes. He throws away 24 bad ones and shares the rest equally among 6 traders. How many tomatoes does each trader get?
Wumpini saves GH₵ 4 every school day for 5 weeks of 5 days. Then she spends GH₵ 35 on sandals in Tolon. How much money does she have left?

math:B4.1.3.1.1.text: The path from Selorm's classroom to the school gate in Hohoe is a line from 0 to 1. Trees split it into 8 equal parts. What fraction is each part? Draw the line and mark 1/8.
A 20 m rope is tied between two poles at a school in Bongo. One pole is 0 and the other is 1. How many metres from 0 are the marks for 1/2, 1/4, 1/5 and 1/10?
On a number line from 0 to 1, Ama of Mampong marks 1/3 and Kofi marks 1/6. Whose mark is closer to 0? Why does the bigger bottom number give the smaller part?

math:B4.1.3.1.2.text: Kwame of Asamankese cuts a sugar cane into 2 equal pieces and eats 1. Adjoa cuts one of the same size into 8 equal pieces. How many must she eat to match Kwame? Write the two fractions.
A fraction chart on a classroom wall in Sunyani shows thirds and sixths. Use a drawing to find how many sixths equal 2/3. Then write one more fraction equal to 2/3.
Adongo ate 3/4 of a pawpaw and Apoka ate 5/8 of one the same size in Navrongo. Change both to eighths, the lowest common denominator. Did they eat the same amount?

math:B4.1.3.1.3.text: Akua sold 12 of the 18 pineapples on her table at Nsawam. Write the fraction sold. Divide the top and bottom by their highest common factor to get the simplest form.
In a class of 40 pupils in Tumu, 16 walk to school. What fraction of the class walks? Give your answer in its simplest form.
A seamstress in Kumasi used 9/12 of a piece of cloth. Owusu says the simplest form is 3/4 and Yaa says it is 3/6. Who is right? Show the factor you divided by.

math:B4.1.3.1.4.text: Mother cuts each orange into 4 equal parts at home in Aburi. Edem eats 11 parts. Write what he ate as an improper fraction and as a mixed number.
A baker in Kasoa cuts each loaf of bread into 6 equal slices. Maku buys 1 whole loaf and 5 more slices. Write this as a mixed number and as an improper fraction.
Draw circles for tins of gari, each split into 3 equal scoops. Shade 7 scoops to show 7/3. How many full tins is that, and how many scoops are left over?

math:B4.1.3.2.1.text: Three friends at Akosombo each have the same size bottle of water. Sena drinks 3/8, Delali drinks 5/8 and Kafui drinks 7/8. Order the fractions from smallest to largest.
Alhassan weeded 3/4 of his plot and Neindow weeded 5/8 of a plot the same size in Savelugu. Change 3/4 to eighths. Who weeded more?
Three taxis in Wa have fuel tanks that are 1/2, 2/3 and 5/6 full. Change them all to sixths, the lowest common denominator, and order them from most fuel to least.

math:B4.1.3.2.3.text: A trader at Makola sells palm oil in a full bottle, a half bottle and a quarter bottle. Ekow needs one and a half bottles. Give two ways he could buy it.
A crate holds 30 eggs. Mama Tiyumba in Sagnarigu buys half a crate and her neighbour buys one-third of a crate. How many eggs does each woman take home?
A school in Jirapa closes at half past one and the bus leaves at a quarter to two. How do the words half and quarter tell you the minutes? How long is the wait?

math:B4.1.4.1.1.text: A tailor in Bechem cuts 7/10 of a metre of ribbon. Write this length as a decimal. Then write 43/100 of a metre as a decimal.
A GH₵ 1 coin is worth 100 pesewas. Write 5 pesewas, 20 pesewas and 65 pesewas as decimal parts of one cedi.
Shade a 10 by 10 grid to show the part of Blay's coconut farm at Half Assini that is planted: 0.36. How many small squares do you shade? Write 0.36 as a fraction.

math:B4.1.4.1.2.text: Atampoka's bag of rice in Bolgatanga weighs 4.67 kg. Round the weight to the nearest tenth of a kilogram.
Three pupils in Dodowa ran 100 m in 18.24, 17.87 and 19.03 seconds. Round each time to the nearest tenth of a second.
A plank at the Sokoban wood market in Kumasi is 2.38 m long. Kwadwo says it is about 2.3 m and Afua says about 2.4 m, to the nearest tenth. Who is right, and why?

math:B4.1.4.1.3.text: Efua buys 0.75 kg of groundnuts and 0.5 kg of beans at Agona Swedru. Line up the decimal points. What is the total weight?
A rope at a Keta fishing beach is 3.4 m long. Mawusi cuts off 1.85 m. How much rope is left? Use a hundredths grid or a number line to explain.
Abane pays GH₵ 2.50 for koko and GH₵ 1.75 for koose in Bawku. How much does he spend? How much change does he get from a GH₵ 5 note?

math:B4.1.5.1.1.text: Out of 100 pupils at a school in Nkwanta, 37 come by bicycle. Write this as a fraction, as a decimal and as a percent.
A cloth seller at Kejetia has a 10 by 10 chart of 100 kente designs. 25 of the squares are gold. What percent is gold? What percent is not gold?
Mahama scored from 9 of his 20 penalty kicks at a school in Salaga. Change 9/20 to hundredths. What percent of his kicks went in?

math:B4.1.5.1.2.text: Three cashew farms near Wenchi have picked part of their crop: farm A 3/5, farm B 0.58 and farm C 65%. Change them all to percents and order them from least to most.
In a spelling quiz in Dzodze, Esinam got 0.7 of the words right, Senyo got 3/4 and Yayra got 72%. Who did best? Who came last?
A water tank at a school in Zebilla was 1/2 full on Monday, 0.45 full on Tuesday and 48% full on Wednesday. Which day had the most water? Put the three in order.

math:B4.2.1.1.1.text: On a hundred chart, Tsatsu of Anloga colours every number he says when he counts in 4s. Describe the pattern the coloured squares make. What do you notice about their last digits?
A chart at a chop bar in Koforidua shows fufu prices: 1 plate GH₵ 25, 2 plates GH₵ 50, 3 plates GH₵ 75. Describe the pattern in words.
Look at the row for 9 on a multiplication chart: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45. Akolgo of Zuarungu sees something in the tens digits and the ones digits. What pattern can you describe?

math:B4.2.1.1.2.text: A trotro fare table at Kaneshie shows: 1 person GH₵ 8, 2 people GH₵ 16, 3 people ?, 4 people GH₵ 32, 5 people ?. Fill in the missing fares and explain how you know.
Bayor's savings table in Wa shows: week 1 GH₵ 15, week 2 GH₵ 30, week 3 GH₵ 45, week 4 ?, week 5 GH₵ 75, week 6 ?. Find the missing amounts.
A chart of orange heaps at Assin Fosu reads 7, 14, ?, 28, 35, ?, 49. Which numbers are missing? What is the rule?

math:B4.2.1.1.3.text: An okada rider in Kintampo charges GH₵ 6 a trip. His table says: 1 trip 6, 2 trips 12, 3 trips 18, 4 trips 26, 5 trips 30. Which entry is wrong? What should it be?
A table for an egg seller in Prestea shows: 1 crate 30 eggs, 2 crates 60, 3 crates 90, 4 crates 110, 5 crates 150. Find the error and correct it.
Naa Lamiley counts balls of kenkey in 3s on a chart: 3, 6, 9, 12, 16, 18, 21. One number breaks the rule. Which is it, and what should it be?

math:B4.2.1.2.1.text: A table shows a pattern: figure 1 has 4 bottle tops, figure 2 has 8 and figure 3 has 12. Build figures 1 to 5 with bottle tops, as Ayisha's class in Gushegu did. How many tops are in figure 5?
A table of oware seeds reads: step 1 has 2 seeds, step 2 has 5, step 3 has 8, step 4 has 11. Lay out seeds or pebbles for each step. What do you add each time? Build step 5.
A table for a kelewele seller in Sunyani shows: 1 wrap has 6 pieces, 2 wraps have 12, 3 wraps have 18. Use paper for wraps and counters for pieces to show 4 wraps. How many counters do you need?

math:B4.2.1.2.2.text: Kwaku in Bekwai lays plantain chips in rows: 2 in the first row, 4 in the second and 6 in the third. Record the rows in a T-chart. How many chips will be in row 10?
Akosua stacks tins of tomato in a shop in Dunkwa: 1 tin on top, 3 in the next layer, 5 in the next. Make a table of layers and tins. How many tins are in layer 6?
A weaver in Bonwire makes kente strips: strip 1 has 5 stripes, strip 2 has 10 and strip 3 has 15. Put this in a T-chart and find the number of stripes on strip 9.

math:B4.2.1.3.1.text: Each tricycle taxi in Bolgatanga has 3 wheels. Make a table for 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 tricycles to show the number of wheels. Explain the rule.
Ama saves GH₵ 2 on Monday. Each day after that she saves double the amount of the day before. Put the days and amounts in a table from Monday to Friday.
A mason in Dambai lays 20 blocks every hour. Draw a table of hours and blocks for the first 6 hours. How many blocks has he laid after 6 hours?

math:B4.2.1.3.2.text: A table shows bags of sachet water sold at a kiosk in Nima: day 1, 5 bags; day 2, 10 bags; day 3, 15 bags. If the pattern goes on, how many bags are sold on day 8? On which day are 60 bags sold?
Kofi's weekly savings in cedis go 4, 8, 12, 16. Esi's go 1, 5, 9, 13. Extend each table by three more weeks. How are the two patterns alike? How are they different?
For a school garden fence in Lawra, 1 section needs 2 poles, 2 sections need 3 poles and 3 sections need 4. Extend the table. How many poles do 15 sections need?

math:B4.2.2.1.1.text: Araba had 24 oranges at her stall in Mankessim. She sold some and has 9 left. Write an equation with a box for the number she sold. Do not solve it yet.
A trotro left Ashaiman with some people. 6 more got on at Tema and now there are 19 on board. Write an equation using a symbol for the number who started the trip.
Fuseina shares some guinea fowl eggs equally into 4 bowls in Savelugu and gets 7 in each bowl. Write an equation with a box or a letter for the unknown number of eggs.

math:B4.2.2.1.2.text: A balance scale at Kete Krachi market has 3 yams and a closed sack on one pan and 11 yams on the other. The pans are level. Write an equation with a symbol for the yams in the sack.
A picture shows Dede's string of beads: 14 red beads, some blue beads hidden under her hand, and 30 beads in all. Write the picture as an equation with a symbol for the hidden beads.
A drawing shows 5 plates with the same number of kelewele pieces on each, and 40 pieces in all. Write an equation with a symbol for the pieces on one plate.

math:B4.2.2.2.1.text: Put 8 bottle tops and a closed tin on one side of a balance and 15 tops on the other, as a class in Ho did. How many tops must be in the tin to make it level? Solve 8 + □ = 15.
Count out 23 groundnuts. Hide some in your hand so that 14 can still be seen. Your friend solves 23 - □ = 14 by counting. How many groundnuts are hidden?
Use pebbles to solve □ + 9 = 21 for Azumah of Garu. Start with 9 pebbles and add one at a time until you have 21. How many did you add?

math:B4.2.2.2.2.text: Yaa of Konongo writes □ - 12 = 30 about her mangoes. Tell a friend in your own words what the box stands for and what the equation says. Then find the number in the box.
A kenkey seller in Tema writes 35 + □ = 80 in her notebook. Say aloud what this could mean for her sales. How would you find the missing number?
In 6 × □ = 48, the box is the number of pupils on each of 6 benches in a Kpandai classroom. Explain in words what the equation tells you. What must the box be?

math:B4.2.2.2.3.text: A shop in Nkoranza had 126 bags of cement and then got some more. Now it has 180 bags. Solve 126 + □ = 180.
Sumaya had some cedis. After paying GH₵ 40 for a school bag in Tamale she has GH₵ 110 left. Solve □ - 40 = 110.
Nyameke needs 75 cocoa pods and has picked 48 on his farm near Elubo. Solve 75 = □ + 48 to find how many more pods he must pick.

math:B4.2.2.2.4.text: Kwesi of Apam guesses numbers for □ - 8 = 9. He tries 15, then 16, then 17. Check each guess. Which one makes the number sentence true?
Fati sold some bowls of tuo zaafi before noon and 7 after noon, 20 in all: □ + 7 = 20. Try 10 as a first guess. Is it too big or too small? Keep trying until it fits.
Use guess and check to solve 4 × □ = 36 for the number of plantains in each of 4 bunches at Kade market. Write down each guess and what it gives.

math:B4.2.2.2.5.text: A trotro from Dunkwa has 23 seats and 14 people are seated. What is unknown here? Write an equation for the empty seats and solve it.
Akua of Juaben needs GH₵ 60 for a football and has saved GH₵ 37. Name the unknown, write an equation with a symbol and solve it by drawing or counting on.
Ziem shared a bag of mangoes equally among 5 friends in Nadowli and each friend got 6. What is the unknown? Write an equation and solve it.

math:B4.2.2.2.6.text: A class in Sandema has 46 pupils and 19 of them are boys. Use a symbol for the number of girls, write the equation and solve it.
Aba of Axim picked 13 coconuts. Her brother Erzuah picked 28 more than she did. Write an equation with a symbol for Erzuah's coconuts and solve it.
After 16 crates of fish were sold at Sekondi harbour, 27 crates were left. Use a symbol for the number of crates at the start. Write the equation and solve it.

math:B4.2.2.2.7.text: Make up a story about buying waakye in Nima that fits 12 + □ = 30. Say what the box stands for in your story, then solve it.
Write a word problem about people in a trotro from Ejisu to Kumasi for 32 - □ = 18. Give it to a friend to solve.
Create a story about sharing mangoes in Bole that matches □ ÷ 3 = 9. Explain what the unknown is and find its value.

math:B4.3.1.1.1.text: Draw half of the Akoma (heart) adinkra symbol on squared paper, with a fold line down the middle. Swap with a partner and draw the other half so that both sides match.
Kweku of Kibi draws the left half of a butterfly on squared paper beside a dotted mirror line. Count squares from the line to draw the right half so the picture is symmetrical.
A teacher in Damongo draws half of a house on a grid: half a square wall and half a triangle roof, next to a line of symmetry. Copy it and finish the house. What shape is the full roof?

math:B4.3.1.1.2.text: Cut a square and a rectangle from old paper, as Adjeley's class in La did. Fold each one to find every line of symmetry. How many does the square have? How many does the rectangle have?
The Ghana flag is a rectangle. Look only at its outline. How many lines of symmetry does the rectangle have? Is a fold from corner to corner one of them?
A kente pattern has four shapes. One triangle has 3 equal sides. One has no equal sides. There is a kite and a slanted parallelogram. Which shapes have a line of symmetry? Draw the lines.

math:B4.3.2.1.1.text: On a map of Ghana, Tamale is north of Kumasi, Cape Coast is south of Kumasi and Ho is to the east. In which direction do you travel from Tamale to Kumasi? From Kumasi to Ho?
On a grid map of a school in Sunyani, the library is 3 squares north of the gate and the canteen is 2 squares west of the gate. Describe how to walk from the canteen to the library.
Atia stands at the flagpole of his school in Bongo. He walks 4 steps north, then 5 steps east, then 4 steps south. In which direction is he from the flagpole now, and how far?

math:B4.3.3.1.1.text: A big step is about 1 m. Kwabena of Mampong walks round his classroom: 8 steps, 6 steps, 8 steps, 6 steps. About what is the perimeter of the room? Why are metres the best unit here?
A finger is about 1 cm wide. Use finger widths to estimate the distance around your maths exercise book, as pupils in Keta did. Then measure with a ruler. How close was your estimate?
An oware board is about 4 hand spans long and 1 hand span wide. Yayra's hand span is about 15 cm. Estimate the perimeter of the board in centimetres.

math:B4.3.3.1.2.text: A vegetable bed at a school in Pusiga has five sides of 4 m, 3 m, 5 m, 2 m and 6 m. What length of fence goes all the way round it?
Measure each side of your desk top with a ruler, as a class in Abetifi did, and record the lengths in centimetres. Add them to find the perimeter.
A square stool top carved in Ahwiaa has sides of 32 cm. What is the distance all the way round the top?

math:B4.3.3.1.3.text: A junior football pitch in Dansoman is 60 m long and 40 m wide. Use perimeter = 2 × (length + width) to find the distance once round the pitch.
A square floor tile in a house in Techiman has sides of 30 cm. Write a rule for the perimeter of any square and use it for this tile.
Rahinatu's groundnut plot in Gushegu is a rectangle with a perimeter of 50 m. It is 15 m long. How wide is it?

math:B4.3.3.1.4.text: Mr Narh has 24 m of fence for a rectangular hen run in Dodowa. Draw three different rectangles with whole-metre sides that use all 24 m. Write the length and width of each.
On 1 cm squared paper, draw two different rectangles for picture frames in a class in Tarkwa. Each must have a perimeter of 20 cm. Do they cover the same number of squares?
Awini of Binduri says only one rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Show that he is wrong by listing at least three such rectangles, starting with 10 cm by 5 cm.

math:B4.3.3.2.1.text: Dzidzor covers a table top in Anloga with square cards of the same size, leaving no gaps. She uses 24 cards. What is the area in card squares? Why must the cards all be one size?
A draughts board at a lorry station in Koforidua has 10 rows of 10 small squares. What is the area of the board in small squares?
On 1 cm squared paper, Kwame of Akim Oda traces a rectangle that covers 3 rows of 7 squares. What is its area? What unit do you write after the number?

math:B4.3.3.2.2.text: Which unit, cm² or m², would you use for the area of a GH₵ 10 note? For the floor of a classroom in Paga? For a maize plot? Give a reason each time.
A fingernail is about 1 cm² and a door laid flat is about 2 m². Which would Ewurabena of Elmina use as a guide for the area of a stamp? Which for a fishing net? Why?
Bukari says the area of his exercise book is 300 m². His teacher in Walewale smiles. What is wrong with his unit? What should it be, and why?

math:B4.3.3.2.3.text: One sleeping mat covers about 2 m². Six mats fit on the floor of Suhuyini's room in Karaga with no space left. Estimate the area of the floor.
A child's palm covers about 50 cm². Azure of Bolgatanga finds that 8 palms cover the lid of a woven basket. About what is the area of the lid?
A big step by a big step is about 1 m². Estimate the area of your classroom floor in m², as pupils in Sefwi Bekwai did. Then measure the length and width to check.

math:B4.3.3.2.4.text: A classroom floor in Nalerigu is 8 m long and 6 m wide. Use area = length × width to find its area.
A square wall tile in a shop in Cape Coast has sides of 20 cm. Find its area. How many cm² do 5 of these tiles cover?
Count the squares in a rectangle 7 squares long and 4 squares wide. Then multiply 7 by 4. What do you notice? Use the rule for Abla's 12 m by 5 m cassava plot in Akatsi.

math:B4.3.3.2.5.text: Madam Serwaa wants a rectangular garden of 36 m² at her house in Bekwai. Give three different pairs of whole-metre length and width that she could use.
On 1 cm squared paper, draw three different rectangles that each cover 18 squares. Tiyumba of Savelugu says they all have the same perimeter. Check if she is right.
30 square tiles can be laid as 5 rows of 6. Lartey, a tiler in Tema, wants other rectangles that use the same 30 tiles. List them all.

math:B4.3.3.3.1.text: A bus leaves Tamale station for Bolgatanga at 14:35. Write this as a 12-hour time with a.m. or p.m. Where do the hands of a wall clock point at that time?
The hour hand on Efia's classroom clock in Obuasi is just past 3 and the minute hand points to 5. What time is it? Write it the way a digital watch shows it.
The news on a radio station in Ho starts at a quarter to seven in the evening. Write this time as a 12-hour digital time and as a 24-hour time.

math:B4.3.3.3.2.text: Senyo leaves home in Kpando at 6:50 a.m. and reaches school at 7:18 a.m. How many minutes does the walk take?
Use a watch with a seconds hand to time a friend skipping 20 times or playing one round of ampe. Record the time in seconds. Is it more or less than 1 minute?
In Afua's kitchen in Berekum, boiling yam took 25 minutes and frying eggs took 240 seconds. Change 240 seconds to minutes. Which took longer, and by how many minutes?

math:B4.3.3.3.3.text: Ghana's Independence Day in 2027 falls on Saturday, 6th March. Write this date in three other ways, such as 06/03/2027.
Farmers' Day in Ghana is the first Friday of December. Find it on this year's calendar and write the date in two different formats.
Mariama from Bimbilla was born on 14.09.16. Write her birthday in words with the full year. How old will she be on 14/09/2027?

math:B4.4.1.1.1.text: A graph in a class in Asamankese shows what pupils ate this morning. Each box is 1 pupil: koko 9 boxes, waakye 7, bread 6, rice water 4. Which food has the most boxes? How many pupils are on the graph?
A graph of games in a Hohoe class uses one face for each pupil: ampe 8 faces, football 11, oware 5 and chaskele 3. How many more pupils chose football than oware?
Each dot on a chart in Lawra stands for one rainy day: May 6 dots, June 9, July 12, August 10. Which month had the fewest rainy days? How many rainy days were in June and July together?

math:B4.4.1.1.2.text: A count at Techiman market found 12 yam sellers, 16 tomato sellers, 8 pepper sellers and 10 onion sellers. One basket picture stands for 2 sellers. How many baskets do you draw for each food?
Class sizes at a school in Half Assini are P1 40, P2 35, P3 45 and P4 30. Draw a pictograph in which one stick figure stands for 5 pupils. How many figures do you draw for P3?
Akua counted at a junction in Suhum: taxis 20, trotros 30, okadas 25 and private cars 15. For her pictograph key, is it better for one wheel to stand for 5 or for 10? Why?

math:B4.4.1.1.3.text: Kwame and Adwoa in Offinso graph the same count of trotros, taxis and bicycles passing their school. Kwame draws a picture graph and Adwoa draws a bar graph. Name two things that are the same and two that are different.
Two graphs show the same goals scored by four school teams in Wa. One has bars going up and the other has bars going across. Does the team with the longest bar change? Explain.
One graph of fish landed at Moree has a picture for every fish. Another has a bar and a number scale. Which is quicker to draw for 48 fish? Do both graphs tell the same story?

math:B4.4.1.1.4.text: Look in a Ghanaian newspaper or on a news website for a pictograph or a bar graph. What does one picture, or one step on the scale, stand for? Tell the class.
A sports page in a Ghanaian newspaper shows goals by four clubs, with one ball for every 5 goals. One club has 7 balls. How many goals is that? What does the key say?
A poster at an education office in Tumu shows school numbers, with one book picture for every 100 pupils. What would 4 and a half books mean? Describe the key in your own words.

math:B4.4.1.2.1.text: Four farmers in Asankragwa sold bags of cocoa: Boakye 20, Pokuaa 45, Yaw 60 and Afriyie 80. Draw a bar graph with a title, labels on both axes and a scale that goes up in 10s.
Books read by Yaa's class in Nkawkaw: stories 12, science 8, poems 4 and history 16. Draw a pictograph with a title, labels and a key. Use one book picture for 4 books.
Selasi's bar graph of trotro, taxi, okada and walking to school in Kadjebi has bars but no title, no labels and no scale. What can a reader not tell? List what she must add.

math:B4.4.1.2.2.text: A pictograph for a kenkey seller in Teshie uses one picture for 10 balls sold: Monday 4 pictures, Tuesday 6, Wednesday 3 and Thursday 5. How many balls did she sell in all?
A bar graph with a scale in 5s shows tree seedlings planted by teams in Bole: Team A 25, Team B 40, Team C 15 and Team D 35. How many more did Team B plant than Team C? What is the total?
Each picture on a chart at Somanya stands for 4 mangoes sold. Maku has 5 pictures and Padi has 3 and a half. How many mangoes did each sell? How many fewer did Padi sell?

math:B5.1.1.1.1.text: A cocoa depot in Sefwi Wiawso stored 524,000 kg of beans. Let a flat stand for 100,000, a rod for 10,000 and a cube for 1,000. How many of each do you need to show 524,000?
On a graph sheet, one small square stands for 1,000 people. A district in the Ashanti Region has 215,000 people. How many squares will Efua shade to show this number?
A school shop club in Tamale counts GH₵ 8,640 in play money. Wumpini has only GH₵ 100 and GH₵ 10 play notes. How many of each make GH₵ 8,640 with the fewest notes?

math:B5.1.1.1.2.text: A radio host in Ho reads out the total of a school fund. It is six hundred and forty-two thousand, three hundred and five cedis. Write this amount in figures.
A signboard at a maize depot in Techiman shows 508,070 kg. Write this number in words. Then write it in expanded form.
Abugri's bus ticket in Bawku has the number 300,000 + 40,000 + 900 + 6. Write the ticket number in figures and read it aloud to a friend.

math:B5.1.1.1.3.text: Akosua in Koforidua makes a chart that counts in 2,500s from 10,000, with 5 numbers in each row. Which numbers come just before and just after 27,500? Which number is right above it?
Number cards on a board at a durbar in Wa go up in 500s: 20,000, 20,500, 21,000 and so on, 10 in a row. Dery's card is 23,500. What numbers are on each side of it and right below it?
A wall chart in a class in Keta counts in 10,000s from 10,000 to 1,000,000, with 10 numbers in a row. Which number is above 450,000? Which is below it? Which two are beside it?

math:B5.1.1.1.4.text: Two yam farmers near Yendi count their tubers. Napari has 48,750 and Suhuyini has 48,570. Write the two numbers with > or < between them. Who has more?
Four trotro stations in Kumasi sold these numbers of tickets in a month: 67,310; 76,130; 67,130; 73,610. Arrange them from the least to the greatest.
A poultry farm in Dormaa Ahenkro collected 92,086 eggs in March, 92,806 in April and 92,608 in May. Order the months from the most eggs to the fewest, using the > sign.

math:B5.1.1.1.5.text: A football match in Tamale had 19,487 fans. Round this number off to the nearest ten, the nearest hundred, the nearest thousand and the nearest ten thousand.
A school in Sunyani needs 2,643 exercise books. The books come in packs of 100. Round 2,643 up to the nearest hundred to find how many to order. Why is rounding down a bad idea here?
A shea butter group in Bole made 38,650 bars of soap one year and 21,280 the next. Round each number to the nearest thousand and estimate the total for the two years.

math:B5.1.1.1.6.text: The meter on a water tanker in Tema goes up by 500 litres at each stop. It now reads 42,350 litres. Write the next five readings.
A cement store in Nkawkaw has 61,000 bags. A truck takes away 1,000 bags on each trip. Count back in 1,000s to show the stock after each of the next six trips.
In a counting game in Navrongo, Apoka counts in 500s: 73,500, 74,000, 74,500, 75,500, 76,000. Which number did she skip? Count on correctly to 78,000.

math:B5.1.1.2.1.text: An old clock at a chapel in Cape Coast shows the hours as I, II, III and so on up to XII. Which numbers do the symbols IV, IX and XII stand for?
Chapters in Yayra's storybook from the Ho library have Roman numerals. She is reading Chapter XL. Is that chapter 40 or 60? Which symbols stand for 1, 5, 10, 50 and 100?
Seats for elders at a durbar in Kumasi are marked XIV, XXV, LXII and XC. Match each seat label to one of these numbers: 90, 14, 62, 25.

math:B5.1.1.2.2.text: Ghana became independent in 1957. In 2026 that is 69 years ago. Write 69 in Roman numerals for a class banner in Goaso.
In a school play in Sekondi, a jersey has the Roman numeral XLVII on the back. What number is it? Write the next number in Roman numerals.
Tetteh in Ada counts canoes on the beach and writes XCIV. His sister Dede counts 88 canoes. Write Tetteh's count in ordinary figures and Dede's count in Roman numerals.

math:B5.1.1.3.1.text: Ama has 36 oranges to sell at Makola Market. She sets them out in equal rows with none left over. List all the ways she can do it and write the factors of 36.
A teacher in Jirapa has 60 pupils for a march past. They must stand in equal rows. Can they stand in rows of 8? List all the factors of 60.
Kwabena packs 48 balls of kenkey into boxes in Winneba. Each box must hold the same number, with none left. Which box sizes can he use? Write every factor of 48.

math:B5.1.1.3.2.text: Enyonam in Kpando has 29 mangoes. She wants equal piles, with more than one pile and more than one mango in a pile. Can she do it? Is 29 prime or composite? Explain.
Houses on a street in Tarkwa are numbered from 40 to 50. Which house numbers are prime? Which are composite?
In an oware club in Mampong, players wear numbers 1 to 20. Players with prime numbers play first. List their numbers. Why is 1 not on your list?

math:B5.1.1.3.3.text: 37 pupils in a class in Tumu line up in twos for assembly. Will every pupil have a partner? Is 37 odd or even? What about a class of 58?
Adwoa sets out 46 tomatoes in rows of two on her table at Obuasi market. Is any tomato left without a pair? Say if 46 is even or odd. Do the same for 75.
Pupils pair up for ampe at a school in Anloga. Count in twos from 2 to find which of these class sizes give everyone a partner: 64, 81, 90, 33.

math:B5.1.1.3.4.text: Mawuli has 42 pens and 56 pencils for pupils in Hohoe. Each pupil gets the same number of pens and the same number of pencils, with none left. Use prime factors to find the largest number of pupils.
A caterer in Sunyani has 24 meat pies, 60 doughnuts and 84 toffees. She makes as many equal party packs as she can and uses everything. Use prime factors to find the HCF of 24, 60 and 84.
Two pieces of kente in Bonwire are 90 cm and 54 cm long. A weaver cuts both into equal strips, as long as possible, with no waste. Use prime factors to find the length of each strip.

math:B5.1.1.3.5.text: Eggs at a farm in Berekum are packed in sixes. Is 84 a multiple of 6? Is 6 then a factor of 84? Explain how the two ideas are linked.
Fati in Walewale says: 8 is a factor of 72, so 72 is a multiple of 8. Is she right? Use the same idea to write one factor of 45 and one multiple of 9 below 100.
Pupils in Elmina sit at tables of 4 for a quiz. Which of these class sizes fill the tables with no one left out: 52, 66, 76, 90? Say how you know if each is a multiple of 4.

math:B5.1.2.1.1.text: A ball of kenkey costs GH₵ 6 in Teshie. Naa knows that 5 balls cost GH₵ 30. Without writing, find the cost of 6 balls and of 7 balls by adding on from the fact she knows.
Each row of a trotro seats 4 people. Kojo knows that 4 rows seat 16 people. Double this to find how many people sit in 8 rows. Explain your thinking.
Zenabu shares 72 groundnut cakes equally among 9 friends in Savelugu. Think: 9 times what number is 72? How many cakes does each friend get?

math:B5.1.2.1.2.text: A bag of sachet water holds 30 sachets. A shop in Madina buys 200 bags. Work out 30 × 200 in your head: multiply 3 by 2, then put back the zeros.
An okada rider in Bolgatanga makes 5 trips a day for 48 days. To find 48 × 5 in your head, halve 48 and double 5. What is the answer?
Efua sells 7 trays of eggs in Cape Coast. Each tray costs GH₵ 59. Find 7 × 59 by working out 7 × 60 and then taking away 7 × 1.

math:B5.1.2.2.1.text: A cocoa farmer near Goaso has 34 rows of trees with 126 trees in each row. How many cocoa trees are on the farm?
A school in Nalerigu buys 45 maths books at GH₵ 38 each. Use the box method or the column method to find the total cost.
A trotro carries 15 passengers on each trip between Kasoa and Accra. It makes 248 trips in a month. How many passengers does it carry that month?

math:B5.1.2.3.1.text: Selorm shares 56 mangoes equally among 8 baskets in Dzodze. How many mangoes go into each basket? Write the multiplication fact that helps you.
81 pupils in Damongo form 9 equal teams for sports day. How many pupils are in each team?
A taxi in Takoradi takes 4 passengers at a time. 36 people are waiting. How many full trips are needed? Can 36 also be divided exactly by 3, 6 and 9?
