math:B5.1.2.4.1.text: A farmer in Atebubu packs 864 tubers of yam into heaps of 6 for the market. How many heaps does he make?
Seven friends in Aflao share GH₵ 945 equally after selling smoked fish. How much does each person get?
A bakery in Nsawam bakes 500 loaves and packs them in crates of 8. How many full crates are there? How many loaves are left over?

math:B5.1.2.5.1.text: Akua buys 3 exercise books at GH₵ 6 each and 2 pens at GH₵ 3 each at a shop in Berekum. She pays with a GH₵ 50 note. How much change does she get?
Mr Ackah, a fisherman in Axim, catches 240 fish. He keeps 24 for his family and packs the rest equally into 9 crates. How many fish are in each crate?
A class of 42 pupils in Wenchi goes on a trip. Each trotro seats 14 pupils and costs GH₵ 250 to hire. How many trotros are needed? What is the total cost?

math:B5.1.2.6.1.text: A fishing net at Elmina hangs 8 m below the sea surface, at -8. The crew pulls it up 5 m. Use a number line to find its new position.
In a quiz in Lawra, a wrong answer scores -3 and a right answer scores +5. Ziem's team gets two wrong answers and then one right answer. What is the team's score?
Korkor owes her friend GH₵ 6, so she writes -6. She borrows GH₵ 4 more to buy waakye. Write this as a sum of two negative numbers and find the answer.

math:B5.1.3.1.1.text: Yaw, Afia and Kwesi each have the same length of sugarcane in Nkoranza. They eat 2/3, 3/4 and 5/8 of it. Find the lowest common denominator of 3, 4 and 8. Then write each as an equivalent fraction.
Half of Dzifa's farm in Kadjebi is planted with cocoa. Write three fractions equal to 1/2 with the denominators 4, 10 and 36.
A water tank at a school in Paga is 3/5 full. The marks on the tank are in twentieths. How many twentieths is 3/5? Show how you got it.

math:B5.1.3.1.2.text: Three trotros wait at Kaneshie. One is 7/10 full, one is 3/5 full and one is 3/4 full. Change them to the same denominator. Order them from the least full to the fullest.
Azure ran 5/8 of the school field in Bolgatanga and Atanga ran 7/12 of it. Change both fractions to the same denominator. Who ran farther?
Akweley ate 2/5 of her kelewele and Lamiokor ate 3/8 of hers. The packs were the same size. Change each fraction to a decimal and say who ate more.

math:B5.1.3.1.3.text: Abena in Ejisu used 1/4 of a bag of rice for jollof on Saturday and 3/8 of the bag on Sunday. What fraction of the bag did she use in all?
A painter in Tema had 5/6 of a tin of paint. He used 1/3 of a tin on a kiosk. What fraction of a tin is left? Give your answer in its simplest form.
Salifu walked 1/2 km from home to the borehole in Tolon and then 3/10 km to school. How far did he walk altogether? Write the answer in its simplest form.

math:B5.1.3.1.4.text: Mrs Boakye bought 2 1/4 yards of wax print and 1 1/2 yards of plain cloth at Kejetia Market. How many yards of cloth did she buy in all?
A container held 4 1/5 litres of palm oil. Maku in Somanya used 1 3/5 litres for stew. Change both to improper fractions and find how much oil is left.
Bukari sent 7/4 tonnes of maize on Monday and 5/2 tonnes on Tuesday to a store in Gushegu. Find the total and write it as a mixed number.

math:B5.1.3.1.5.text: Each of 5 children in Akosombo drinks 3/4 of a cup of koko. Draw the cups and shade them. How many cups of koko do they drink in all?
Kafui sews 4 dresses in Keta. Each dress needs 2 1/2 yards of cloth. Work out 4 × 2 1/2 by finding 4 × 2 and 4 × 1/2 and adding them.
A banku seller in Dambai uses 2/5 of a bag of corn dough each day. Use a number line to show how much dough she uses in 6 days.

math:B5.1.3.1.6.text: Memunatu has 24 guinea fowl eggs in Savelugu. She sells 2/3 of them. Draw 24 eggs, put them in 3 equal groups and find how many she sells.
Three quarters of the 40 pupils in a class in Bibiani walk to school. How many pupils walk? Show it with a drawing or a bar.
Nii has 4 equal sticks of sugarcane in Teshie. He gives away 3/5 of each stick. Use a drawing to find 3/5 × 4. How much sugarcane does he give away?

math:B5.1.4.1.1.text: A bag of groundnuts in Bawku weighs 0.375 kg. Write 0.375 as a fraction with 1,000 as the denominator. How many tenths, hundredths and thousandths does it have?
Delali walks 5/8 km to school in Kpando. Change 5/8 to thousandths and write the distance as a decimal.
A metre stick in a class in Wa is marked in millimetres, so each mark is 1/1000 of a metre. Lariba's pencil reaches the 147th mark. Write its length in metres as a decimal and as a fraction.

math:B5.1.4.1.2.text: Three girls ran 100 m at a school in Sekondi. Their times were 14.325 s, 14.235 s and 14.352 s. Order the times from the fastest to the slowest.
Edem's bottle holds 0.75 litre of sobolo and Senyo's holds 4/5 litre. Write 4/5 as a decimal. Then put <, > or = between the two amounts.
Three bags of shea nuts in Gambaga weigh 0.87 kg, 7/8 kg and 0.857 kg. Change 7/8 to a decimal. Then order the weights from the lightest to the heaviest.

math:B5.1.4.1.3.text: A baby at a clinic in Nandom weighs 4.286 kg. Round the weight to the nearest tenth of a kilogram and to the nearest hundredth.
An okada rider in Aburi buys 3.647 litres of fuel. Round this to the nearest hundredth of a litre. Then round 3.647 to the nearest tenth.
Ayine shares 2 m of rope equally among 3 friends in Navrongo. A calculator shows 0.6666 m for each friend. Write each share to the nearest hundredth of a metre.

math:B5.1.4.1.4.text: Araba buys 0.875 kg of tilapia and 0.45 kg of shrimps at the Elmina fish market. Line up the decimal points and find the total weight.
A bottle holds 1.5 litres of palm oil. Dede in Kpong pours out 0.375 litre for soup. How much oil is left in the bottle?
Fuseini cycles 2.75 km from Tolon to his farm and then 1.085 km to the dam. How far does he cycle in all? How much longer is the first part than the second?

math:B5.1.4.1.5.text: One sachet of water holds 0.5 litre. A football team in Yendi drinks 12 sachets after a match. Show on a number line how many litres they drink.
A tin of tomato paste weighs 0.21 kg. A chop bar in Nkawkaw buys 8 tins. Multiply 21 by 8, then place the decimal point to find the total weight.
A bead maker in Odumase Krobo uses 0.125 m of string for each bracelet. How much string does she need for 6 bracelets?

math:B5.1.5.1.1.text: A class in Juaboso has 60 pupils. 35% of them come to school by bicycle. How many pupils is that?
Akosua has 80 plantain suckers to plant on her farm near Bechem. She plants 40% of them on Monday. Change 40% to a fraction and find how many suckers she plants.
Mahama scored 18 out of 25 in a maths test in Salaga. What percentage did he score?

math:B5.1.5.1.2.text: A yam seller in Kintampo had 48 tubers and sold 25% of them by noon. What fraction is 25%? Use it to find how many tubers she sold.
A bus from Wa to Tumu has 35 seats and 40% of them are empty. First estimate using 50%. Then use 20% = 1/5 to find the exact number of empty seats.
Match each fraction to its percentage: 1/2, 1/4, 3/4, 1/10, 1/5 and 10%, 75%, 20%, 50%, 25%. Then find 75% of the 80 cocoa pods Osei picked in Enchi.

math:B5.1.5.1.3.text: A shop in Koforidua sells a school bag for GH₵ 80. On market day there is 25% off. How much is taken off? What is the new price?
Tiyumba's phone in Tamale shows 40% battery. A full charge lasts 20 hours. About how many hours of use are left?
A circle graph shows how 40 pupils in a class in Axim come to school: 50% walk, 25% take a trotro and 25% ride bicycles. How many pupils are in each group?

math:B5.2.1.1.1.text: A weaver in Kpetoe counts her kente strips at the end of each week: 20, 40, 60, 80. Write the next three numbers. How does each number differ from the one before it?
Awini saves in a susu box in Zebilla. The total after each week is GH₵ 50, GH₵ 100, GH₵ 150, GH₵ 200. Extend the pattern to week 8 and explain how it grows.
A number line on a classroom wall in Jasikan shows 2,500, 3,000, 3,500, __, __, 5,000. Fill in the missing numbers. What is added each time?

math:B5.2.1.1.2.text: A farmer in Wenchi builds a fence. 2 posts need 1 rail, 3 posts need 2 rails and 4 posts need 3 rails. Describe in words how the number of rails is linked to the number of posts.
Asibi fries plantain in Bolgatanga. For 1, 2, 3 and 4 customers she fries 3, 5, 7 and 9 slices. Use words like 'twice' and 'more than' to describe the pattern.
Tables are joined end to end for a party in Tema. The seats go 6, 11, 16, 21 as each table is added. Describe in writing how the number of seats changes each time.

math:B5.2.1.1.3.text: Kabenla stacks tins of fish at Half Assini market: 1 tin in the top row, 3 in the next row and 5 in the next. Predict how many tins are in the 4th and 5th rows. State the rule.
A trotro fare from Suhum grows with the trip: 2 stops cost GH₵ 4, 3 stops cost GH₵ 6 and 4 stops cost GH₵ 8. Predict the fare for 5 stops and for 9 stops.
Esi plaits hair in Swedru. She has made 4 braids after 5 minutes, 8 after 10 minutes and 12 after 15 minutes. Predict the number of braids after 20 and after 25 minutes.

math:B5.2.1.1.4.text: Ekow in Saltpond makes squares in a row with broomsticks: 1 square uses 4 sticks and 2 squares use 7. He predicts 5 squares need 16 sticks. Draw the pattern to check. Is he right?
Bottle tops are set out as squares on a desk in Nkwanta: 1, then 4, then 9. Senyo predicts the 5th square needs 20 tops. Draw the 4th and 5th squares to check his prediction.
Oranges are stacked in a triangle at Agbogbloshie market: 1 on top, then 2, then 3 in each row. Rahinatu predicts that 6 rows need 21 oranges. Draw the stack to check.

math:B5.2.1.1.5.text: Tsotsoo saves in a susu box in Osu. She puts in GH₵ 1.50 in week 1, GH₵ 3.00 in week 2 and GH₵ 4.50 in week 3. If the pattern goes on, how much does she put in during week 6?
A water tank in Kenyasi holds 960 litres. Each day, half of the water left is used: 960, 480, 240. How much water is left after two more days?
In a clapping game in Lawra, the claps in each round are 5, 8, 13, 20. The jump grows by 2 each round. How many claps are in round 5 and in round 6?

math:B5.2.1.1.6.text: Kwaku puts oranges in heaps at Ejura market: 3, 6, 9, 12, 16. His sister says one heap breaks the pattern. Which heap is wrong? What should it be? Explain.
Bus tickets at Hohoe station are numbered 105, 110, 115, 120. Mawuli says the next ticket is 130. Is he right? Explain using the rule.
A drummer in Tamale beats 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 times in each round. Sumaya says the next round has 32 beats. Issah says 24. Who is right, and why?

math:B5.2.1.1.7.text: A tray holds 30 eggs. On a farm in Dormaa Ahenkro, 1 tray has 30 eggs, 2 trays have 60 and 3 trays have 90. Write the rule for n trays in words and in algebra.
A taxi in Sunyani charges GH₵ 5 to start and GH₵ 3 for each kilometre: GH₵ 8 for 1 km, GH₵ 11 for 2 km, GH₵ 14 for 3 km. Write the rule for n km in words and as an expression.
Kelewele costs GH₵ 5 a pack in Dansoman, but the first pack each day is free: 1 pack costs GH₵ 0, 2 packs GH₵ 5, 3 packs GH₵ 10. Write the cost of n packs in words and in algebra.

math:B5.2.1.1.8.text: A table at a tailor's shop in Ho shows the cost of sewing school uniforms: 1 costs GH₵ 40, 2 cost GH₵ 80, 3 cost GH₵ 120. Write an expression for n uniforms. How many were sewn if the bill is GH₵ 600?
A table of okada fares in Bawku shows: 2 km costs GH₵ 6, 3 km costs GH₵ 9 and 5 km costs GH₵ 15. Write an expression for the fare for k km. Use it to find the fare for 8 km.
A table shows pencils sent to classes in Nkoranza: a class of 20 gets 25, a class of 30 gets 35 and a class of 42 gets 47. Write an expression for a class of p pupils. How many for 55 pupils?

math:B5.2.2.1.1.text: A ball of banku costs b cedis in Aflao. A fish costs GH₵ 7 more than a ball of banku. Write an expression for the cost of the fish and for the cost of 4 balls of banku.
A rectangular maize plot near Ejura is x metres long and 5 metres wide. Write an expression for the distance around it and simplify it.
Kojo sells m mangoes in the morning and 5m mangoes in the afternoon at Somanya. Write the total as one term. Find the total when m = 12.

math:B5.2.3.1.1.text: Serwaa pays GH₵ 20 for a pen and a maths set in Bechem. The pen costs GH₵ 3.50 and the maths set costs m cedis. Write an equation with m for this problem.
Mensah has GH₵ 6 in his susu box in Asankragwa and adds GH₵ 3 every week. Write an equation for his savings s after w weeks. How much will he have after 10 weeks?
Hawa packs 96 balls of shea butter into boxes of 8 in Tumu. Let b stand for the number of boxes. Write an equation that shows this.

math:B5.2.3.1.2.text: Adjoa had some toffees. Her aunt in Nungua gave her 7 more and now she has 22. What is the unknown? Write an equation with a letter and solve it.
Four equal bags of gari sit on a scale at Techiman market. The scale reads 20 kg. Write an equation for the weight w of one bag and solve it.
A trotro left Cape Coast with 32 passengers. Some got off at Mankessim and 19 were left. Write an equation for the number who got off and solve it.

math:B5.2.3.1.3.text: Write a short story about buying kenkey and fish in Jamestown that fits the equation 6 + k = 15. Say what k stands for in your story and find its value.
The equation 4n = 28 is on the board in a class in Bole. Make up a market problem about heaps of tomatoes that this equation could stand for. What does n mean?
Make up two different stories for the equation 20 - y = 12. One is about passengers on a trotro in Kumasi. The other is about change from a GH₵ 20 note. Then solve for y.

math:B5.3.1.1.1.text: Look at the Ghana flag and a square floor tile. Which one is a rectangle but not a square? Give reasons using their sides and angles.
A draughts board at a taxi rank in Koforidua is a square. How many equal sides and how many right angles does it have? If one diagonal is 40 cm long, how long is the other?
A football pitch in Bibiani is 100 m long and 64 m wide. Name its shape. Which sides are equal and parallel? How many right angles does it have? Are its two diagonals equal?

math:B5.3.1.1.2.text: Dzifa in Hohoe cuts a square from an old calendar. She folds it along both diagonals. Do the fold lines cut each other in half? Do they meet at right angles? Try it and see.
Cut out a paper rectangle shaped like the Ghana flag. Fold it so that one short side lies on the other. What does this show about the opposite sides? Fold again to test the long sides.
Yaw in Mampong folds a paper rectangle along one diagonal. The two halves do not cover each other. He does the same with a square and they do. What does this tell him about the two shapes?

math:B5.3.1.1.3.text: A road sign at a junction in Takoradi has 8 sides. Akua measures each side as 30 cm and each angle as 135 degrees. Is the sign a regular polygon? Explain.
A kite flown at Labadi beach has four sides of 25 cm each, but its angles are 60, 120, 60 and 120 degrees. Is the kite a regular polygon? Give a reason.
Narh in Ada cuts a paper triangle with sides of 12 cm, 12 cm and 12 cm. How can he fold it to check that all its angles are equal? Is it a regular polygon?

math:B5.3.2.1.1.text: Kwesi's pace is about 1 m. He walks round a classroom block in Assin Fosu: 28 paces along and 9 paces across. Estimate the perimeter. A tape gives 27 m by 8.5 m. Find the real perimeter and compare.
Abena's thumb is about 1 cm wide. Her maths set tin in Obuasi is about 18 thumbs long and 6 thumbs wide. Estimate its perimeter. A ruler gives 17.5 cm by 6 cm. Find the real perimeter and compare.
Use your hand span to estimate the perimeter of an oware board or your desk top. Then measure each side with a ruler and add. How far apart are your estimate and the measured perimeter?

math:B5.3.2.1.2.text: A school garden in Kadjebi is a rectangle 24 m long and 15 m wide. How many metres of fence are needed to go all the way round it?
A triangular road sign near Nkawkaw has three sides of 60 cm each. Find its perimeter in centimetres. Then write it in metres.
An L-shaped compound in Navrongo has sides of 12 m, 5 m, 7 m, 4 m, 5 m and 9 m. Find the distance around the compound.

math:B5.3.2.1.3.text: The floor of a chop bar in Sunyani is made of two rectangles. One is 8 m by 5 m and the other is 4 m by 3 m. Find the total floor area in square metres.
Afua's farm near Nsawam is L-shaped. It can be split into a rectangle 30 m by 20 m and a rectangle 10 m by 15 m. What is the area of the whole farm?
A T-shaped paper badge for a school in Wa is made from a strip 12 cm by 3 cm on top of a strip 4 cm by 9 cm. Find the area of the badge in square centimetres.

math:B5.3.2.2.1.text: Which is closer to 1 cubic centimetre: a cube of sugar or a tin of milk? Which is closer to 1 cubic metre: a big water tank at a house in Kasoa or a bucket? Give reasons.
Amina wants to measure the space inside a kenkey seller's ice chest in Kintampo and the space inside a classroom. Which unit fits each one, cm³ or m³? Explain your choice.
A cube box at Tema port is 1 m long, 1 m wide and 1 m high. How many 1 cm cubes fit along one edge? How many 1 cm³ cubes would fill the whole box?

math:B5.3.2.2.2.text: Kwame in Bekwai fills a small box with 1 cm cubes. The bottom layer has 4 rows of 6 cubes, and 5 layers fill the box. What is the volume of the box in cm³?
A box for shea butter soap in Damongo is 10 cm long, 5 cm wide and 3 cm high. How many 1 cm³ cubes would fill it? Use length × width × height.
Sugar cubes of 1 cm³ are packed in a box in Akim Oda: 8 along the length, 5 across and 4 high. How many cubes are in the full box? What is its volume?

math:B5.3.2.2.3.text: Senam in Sogakope has 24 cubes of 1 cm³. She wants to build a solid box that uses all of them. Write three different sets of length, width and height she can use.
A toffee maker in Kumasi packs 36 cube toffees of 1 cm³ in a box with no gaps. Give the length, width and height of two different boxes that hold exactly 36. Which box is flatter?
Two boxes in a shop in Yeji measure 2 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm and 1 cm by 6 cm by 5 cm. Do they have the same volume? Find a third box with that volume.

math:B5.3.2.2.4.text: A cube tin 10 cm long, 10 cm wide and 10 cm high is filled with palm oil in Assin Fosu. What is its volume in cm³? How many litres of oil does it hold?
A water tank at a clinic in Nalerigu has a volume of 2 m³. If 1 m³ holds 1,000 litres, what is the capacity of the tank in litres?
A sobolo seller in Madina has a box-shaped cooler. Inside it is 20 cm by 10 cm by 15 cm. Find its volume in cm³. How many litres of sobolo can it hold?

math:B5.3.3.3.1.text: Ama opens her classroom door in Konongo a little, then to a square corner, then wide. For each position, say if the angle at the hinge is less than, equal to or greater than a right angle.
Fold a sheet of paper twice to make a right-angle tester. Use it on a corner of the Ghana flag, the tip of a slice of pawpaw and the open blades of scissors. Sort the angles into three groups.
At 3 o'clock the hands of the clock at a lorry station in Wa make a right angle. Is the angle between the hands at 1 o'clock smaller or larger than a right angle? What about at 5 o'clock?

math:B5.3.3.3.2.text: Kofi in Akropong measures two angles. The angle at the top of a roof is 110 degrees. The angle between a ladder and the ground is 65 degrees. Is each angle acute, right, obtuse or reflex?
Draw clock hands showing 4 o'clock, like the wall clock of a school in Bimbilla. Measure the smaller angle with your protractor. What type of angle is it? What type is the larger angle?
Use a protractor to draw angles of 35, 90, 125 and 300 degrees for a sketch map of roads in Kete Krachi. Label each angle acute, right, obtuse or reflex.

math:B5.3.4.1.1.text: Look at a map of Ghana. Is Bolgatanga north or south of Kumasi? Is Ho east or west of Koforidua? Is Cape Coast east or west of Accra?
On a grid map of a town, the chief's palace is 3 squares east and 2 squares north of the market. Yaa is at the palace. Give her directions to walk back to the market.
From the school gate in Wenchi, Kwabena walks 4 squares north on a grid and then 5 squares east to the clinic. Next he walks 4 squares south. Where is he now from the school gate?

math:B5.3.4.2.2.text: A canoe on Keta Lagoon is seen upside down in the still water. The water line is the mirror line. The tip of its flag is 2 m above the water. How far below the water line is the image of the tip?
An Adinkra stamp makes a print on cloth in Ntonso. The print is the mirror image of the stamp. If a mark is on the left of the stamp, where is it on the print? Do the size and shape change?
A triangle on a grid is 2 squares to the left of a mirror line. Esinam in Denu draws its image 3 squares to the right of the line. Is her image correct? Where should it be, and should it be flipped?

math:B5.4.1.1.1.text: Adongo counts the vehicles that pass his school gate in Bolgatanga for one hour. Azure reads the number of vehicles in a newspaper report. Who has first-hand data and who has second-hand data? Why?
Araba asks 30 classmates in Saltpond for their favourite food and tallies the answers. Later a pupil in another school uses her table. For whom is it first-hand data? For whom is it second-hand?
Sort these into first-hand and second-hand data. Prices you ask for yourself at Kaneshie Market. A league table in a newspaper. Heights you measure in class. Rainfall figures from a website.

math:B5.4.1.1.2.text: A newspaper table shows points for four school teams: Wa 12, Tamale 15, Ho 9, Sunyani 15. Is this first-hand or second-hand data for you? Which teams are level? Write one more question about it.

A price list on a radio station's website gives the cost of a tuber of yam in three markets: Techiman GH₵ 18, Kumasi GH₵ 25, Accra GH₵ 30. Where is yam cheapest? How much more is it in Accra than in Techiman?
Other people collect data that you can use. Name three places to find such data, like a newspaper in Ghana, a school notice board or a website. Say what each set of data is about.

math:B5.4.1.2.1.text: Osei and Mariama sell maize in Ejura. On Monday they sold 12 and 9 bags. On Tuesday they sold 15 and 18. On Wednesday they sold 10 and 14. Draw a double bar graph with a title, labelled axes and a key.
Elikem and Yayra in Akatsi took three tests. In Maths they scored 70% and 85%. In English, 80% and 75%. In Science, 65% and 90%. Draw a double bar graph. In which subject is the gap the biggest?
Boys and girls in three classes of a school in Jirapa: B4 has 18 boys and 22 girls, B5 has 20 and 20, B6 has 25 and 19. Draw a double bar graph with a key. Which class has more girls than boys?

math:B5.4.1.2.2.text: A newspaper graph has two bars for each month: one for cocoa bought in Sefwi Wiawso and one for cocoa bought in Goaso. What does the key tell you? Why is this called a double bar graph?

A double bar graph on the TV news shows goals scored and goals let in by a team from Cape Coast in three matches: 2 and 1, 0 and 3, 4 and 2. In which match did it score the most? How many goals did it let in altogether?
Look in an old newspaper or magazine in Ghana for a graph with two bars side by side. Write its title, what each colour of bar stands for and one fact you can read from it.

math:B5.4.2.1.1.text: A basket in Agogo holds only oranges and mangoes. Pokuaa picks one fruit without looking. Is each pick impossible, possible or certain? An orange. A pawpaw. An orange or a mango.
A spinner for a class game in Yendi has the numbers 2, 4, 6 and 8. Say if each event is impossible, possible or certain. It lands on an even number. It lands on 5. It lands on 8.
Say if each event is impossible, possible or certain. 6 March next year will be Independence Day in Ghana. It will rain in Tamale next Friday. A hen in Bawku will lay a mango.

math:B5.4.2.1.2.text: Wumpini puts 12 groundnuts, 3 tiger nuts and 1 bean in a calabash. A friend picks one without looking. Which pick is likely, which is unlikely, which is impossible and which is certain? Test it 20 times.
Design a spinner with 8 equal parts for an ampe team draw. Landing on blue must be likely, red unlikely and green impossible. How will you colour the parts? Spin it 16 times and record the results.

Afriyie in Bechem has 9 oranges and 1 mango in a sack. She picks one fruit without looking and puts it back. Write one outcome that is certain, one likely, one unlikely and one impossible. Then try it 10 times.

math:B5.4.2.1.3.text: Toss a 50 pesewas coin 20 times with a partner. Before you start, predict the number of heads. Record each toss in a tally table. Was your prediction close? Explain what you found.
Roll a ludo die 30 times, as pupils in Kpandai do at break. Tally how many times each number shows. Did every number show the same number of times? Why might the results differ?
Put 3 red and 1 blue bottle tops in a bag. Pick one, record its colour and put it back. Do this 20 times. Abugri in Garu picked red 14 times. Is that close to what you would expect? Explain.

math:B6.1.1.1.1.text: A cocoa depot in Sefwi Wiawso counted 352,000 beans. With base blocks, a flat stands for 100,000, a rod for 10,000 and a small cube for 1,000. Which pieces would you lay out to show this number?
The people of Yendi raised GH₵ 240,000 for a new clinic. On a graph sheet, one small square stands for GH₵ 1,000. How many squares must you shade to show the amount?
A bank in Takoradi pays out GH₵ 123,400 using only GH₵ 100 notes. How many notes is that? How many GH₵ 200 notes would make GH₵ 600,000?

math:B6.1.1.1.2.text: The 2021 census counted 30,832,019 people in Ghana. Write this number in words. What is the value of the digit 8 in it?
A radio presenter in Koforidua says a new road will cost two hundred and five million, sixty thousand cedis. Write this amount in figures.
A water factory in Tema filled 4,075,300 sachets last year. Write this number in expanded form to show the value of each digit.

math:B6.1.1.1.3.text: Elikem in Hohoe makes a number chart that goes up by 1,500 along each row and by 10,000 down each column. He points to 24,500. Which numbers are to its left, to its right, above it and below it?
On a chart in Azara's class in Walewale, numbers go up by 2,000 across and by 20,000 down. What number is two steps to the right of 46,000? What number is one step below 46,000?
Kojo of Saltpond covers one number on a chart. The number on its left is 58,500 and the number on its right is 61,500. Numbers go up by 1,500 across. Which number did he cover?

math:B6.1.1.1.4.text: A football match in Kumasi drew 38,450 fans and one in Accra drew 38,540 fans. Write the two numbers with < or > between them. Which city had the bigger crowd?
Four farmer groups near Techiman harvested 72,300 kg, 27,900 kg, 72,030 kg and 70,950 kg of maize. Put the harvests in order from the smallest to the largest.
Dzifa's shop in Keta sold goods worth GH₵ 84,600 last year. Senyo's shop sold GH₵ 10,000 less. How much did Senyo's shop sell? Compare the two amounts using < or >.

math:B6.1.1.1.5.text: A festival in Winneba drew 46,738 visitors. Round this number off to the nearest ten, hundred, thousand and ten thousand.
A yam trader in Bimbilla has 23,460 tubers. Round this number up to the nearest thousand, then round it down to the nearest thousand. Which answer is closer to the real number?
Bawku market had 18,790 shoppers on Friday and 21,240 on Saturday. Round each number off to the nearest thousand, then estimate the total for the two days.

math:B6.1.1.1.6.text: A poultry farm at Dormaa Ahenkro packs 5,000 eggs each day. It has packed 285,000 so far. Count on in 5,000s to find the total after each of the next five days.
A water tank in Tumu holds 830,000 litres. The town uses 10,000 litres a day and no water is added. Count back in 10,000s for six days. How much water is left?
Naa Dei of Teshie counts in 5,000s: 615,000, 620,000, 625,000, 635,000, 640,000. She has left out one number. Which number is missing?

math:B6.1.1.2.1.text: The clock on an old church tower in Cape Coast shows the hour IX. A stone on the wall has the number XL. Which numbers do these two Roman numerals stand for?
The chapters of a storybook at a school in Obuasi have Roman numerals. Yaw is on chapter XVI and Akua is on chapter XIX. Write both chapters as ordinary numbers. Who has read further?
Mrs Lamptey in Nungua writes I, V, X, L and C on the board. What number does each letter stand for? Which letter stands for 50?

math:B6.1.1.2.2.text: On 6 March 2026 Ghana marked 69 years of independence. Write 69 in Roman numerals. Then write the Roman numeral for 70.
Awuni's grandmother in Zebilla is LXXIV years old and his little sister is VIII. Write both ages in ordinary numbers. How many years older is the grandmother?
Efua in Komenda sets a puzzle for her friend: XXIV + ? = XL. Find the missing number and write it as a Roman numeral.

math:B6.1.1.3.1.text: Adwoa in Nkawkaw has 42 oranges and 70 mangoes. She packs them into baskets that all hold the same mix, with no fruit left. Use prime factors to find the largest number of baskets she can make.
At Sunyani station, a trotro leaves for Berekum every 12 minutes. One leaves for Techiman every 18 minutes. Both leave at 6:00 a.m. Use prime factors to find when they next leave together.
Tiyumba in Savelugu has ropes of 24 m, 60 m and 84 m. She cuts all of them into equal pieces, as long as possible, with nothing left over. Use prime factors to find the length of one piece.

math:B6.1.2.1.1.text: Kelewele is sold in packs of 7 pieces at a stall in Osu. Maku knows that 5 packs hold 35 pieces. How can she use this fact to find the number of pieces in 6 packs and in 7 packs?
A bag of oranges costs GH₵ 9 at Agbogbloshie market. For 6 bags, Kwei thinks: 10 sixes, then take away 6. Show his working. Use the same idea to find 9 × 8.
Apoka in Navrongo has 72 pieces of kulikuli to share equally among 8 friends. She thinks, '8 times what makes 72?' How many pieces does each friend get?

math:B6.1.2.1.2.text: A crate holds 30 eggs. A shop in Koforidua buys 400 crates. Work out 4 × 3 first, then add the zeros to find 400 × 30 in your head. How many eggs is that?
Mawuli sells 32 balls of kenkey at GH₵ 5 each in Aflao. To work it out in his head, he halves 32 and doubles 5. Show how this works and find the money he collects.
A bowl of tuo zaafi costs GH₵ 16 at a chop bar in Tamale. Find the cost of 7 bowls by splitting 16 into 10 and 6. If a bowl cost GH₵ 19, how would 20 - 1 help you?

math:B6.1.2.2.1.text: A school in Goaso buys 245 maths books at GH₵ 36 each. How much does the school pay altogether?
A cocoa farm near Enchi has 128 rows with 235 trees in each row. How many cocoa trees are on the farm?
A bus makes 46 trips in a month between Wa and Tamale. Each trip is about 310 km. About how many kilometres does the bus travel in the month?

math:B6.1.2.3.1.text: Ayine in Bolgatanga weaves 63 baskets and ties them in bundles of 9 for the market. How many bundles does he make? Which times-table fact helps you?
In a game of oware in Offinso, Akosua has 48 seeds to drop equally into 6 pits. How many seeds go into each pit? How many would go into each of 8 pits?
A baker in Kasoa has 78 loaves of bread. Can she pack all of them in trays of 6 with none left over? Use a divisibility rule, not long division, to decide.

math:B6.1.2.4.1.text: A farmer in Kete Krachi packs 864 yams into crates of 6. How many crates does he fill?
Seven friends in Half Assini earn GH₵ 945 from selling coconuts and share it equally. How much does each friend get?
A school in Jasikan has 500 exercise books to share equally among 8 classes. How many books does each class get, and how many are left over?

math:B6.1.2.5.1.text: Esi buys 3 balls of kenkey at GH₵ 6 each and fried fish for GH₵ 15 in Mankessim. She pays with a GH₵ 50 note. How much change does she get?
A farmer in Wenchi picks 480 mangoes. He keeps 30 for his family and packs the rest equally into 9 boxes. How many mangoes go into each box?
A trotro mate in Ashaiman collects GH₵ 8 from each of 15 riders on every trip. After 4 trips the driver spends GH₵ 220 on fuel. How much money is left?

math:B6.1.2.6.1.text: A cold store at Tema harbour keeps fish at -18°C. The room next to it is at -5°C. Mark both numbers on a number line. Which room is colder? Write the comparison using < or >.
In a quiz in Lawra, each wrong answer takes away a point. The scores are Dery 3, Ziem -2, Bayor -5 and Tengan 0. Put the scores in order from the lowest to the highest.
Kafui in Ho marks -7 and 4 on a number line. Which integer is the opposite of 4? Which is greater, -7 or -4? How many steps is it from -7 to 4?

math:B6.1.2.6.2.text: Nii Lante of La owes his friend GH₵ 8, so he writes -8. Then he earns GH₵ 5 for washing a taxi and pays it to his friend. Work out -8 + 5. Does he still owe money?
A cold room for fish in Sekondi is at -6°C. A worker turns it down by 7 degrees. Work out -6 - 7 to find the new temperature.
In a spelling game in Kpando, Akpene has 4 points and then loses 9 points. Work out 4 - 9. Next, find the number you must add to 6 to get -10.

math:B6.1.2.6.3.text: Fuseini in Sagnarigu borrows GH₵ 4 from his sister on each of 3 days. Show each loan as -4. Use hops on a number line to work out 3 × (-4). What does the answer tell you?
A cold store in Apam starts at 0°C and gets 2 degrees colder every hour. Work out 5 × (-2) to find the temperature after 5 hours.
In a quiz in Bechem, each wrong answer scores -3. Abena gets 6 answers wrong. Write a multiplication sentence and find her score from these answers.

math:B6.1.3.1.1.text: Three farmers at Asesewa sold part of their maize. Tetteh sold 3/5 of his, Dede sold 65% of hers and Korkor sold 0.58 of hers. Change all three to one form. Who sold the largest share?
In a test in Salaga, Mariama got 7/8 of the marks, Issah got 85% and Zenabu got 0.9 of the marks. Put the three scores in order from the lowest to the highest.
Three equal water tanks in Nkwanta are 0.625 full, 3/4 full and 70% full. Place the three amounts on a number line from 0 to 1. Which tank holds the least water?

math:B6.1.3.1.2.text: Yaa in Ejisu mixes 2 1/2 cups of gari with 1 2/3 cups of cooked beans. How many cups of food does she have altogether?
A tailor in Dzodze has 5 1/4 yards of cloth. She uses 2 2/3 yards to sew a dress. How many yards of cloth are left?
Sulemana walks 3/4 km from home to the mosque in Yendi and then 5/6 km to school. How far does he walk in all? How much longer is the second part than the first?

math:B6.1.3.1.3.text: Each of 5 children in Dodowa gets 3/4 of a ball of banku. Draw a picture to show 5 × 3/4. How many balls of banku is that altogether?
Araba has 12 pineapples at her stall near Nsawam. She sells 2/3 of them before noon. Use a drawing to find 2/3 of 12.
Half of a school garden in Jirapa is for vegetables. Okro takes up 3/4 of the vegetable part. Shade a paper rectangle to find what fraction of the whole garden grows okro.

math:B6.1.4.1.1.text: A class in Bibiani has 18 girls and 12 boys. Write the ratio of girls to boys, then give it in its simplest form.
Amihere in Axim mixes 2 cups of pineapple juice with 6 cups of water. Write the ratio of juice to water in its simplest form. What fraction of the whole drink is juice?
A small drum at a borehole in Nadowli holds 40 litres and a big drum holds 200 litres. How many small drums fill the big one? Write the ratio of small to big in the form 1 : n.

math:B6.1.4.1.2.text: Selorm in Kpeve stirs 2 spoons of cocoa powder into 5 cups of water. Enyonam stirs 3 spoons into 8 cups. Whose drink has the stronger cocoa taste? Use equal ratios to explain.
The ratio of goats to sheep on a farm near Tumu is 3 : 5. There are 27 goats. How many sheep are there? How many animals are there altogether?
A waakye seller at Kejetia cooks rice and beans in the ratio 4 : 1. How many cups of beans does she need for 12 cups of rice? Complete 4 : 1 = 12 : ?

math:B6.1.4.2.1.text: One oware board has 12 pits. Draw a mapping from 1, 2, 3 and 5 boards to their number of pits. Write two of the pairs as equal ratios. Is the number of pits proportional to the number of boards?
At a stall in Atebubu, 2 tubers of yam cost GH₵ 30, 4 tubers cost GH₵ 60 and 6 tubers cost GH₵ 80. Check the ratio of cost to tubers each time. Is the cost proportional? Explain.
At a store in Ejura, 40 equal sacks hold 2,000 kg of maize. How much maize is in one sack? How much maize would 7 sacks hold?

math:B6.1.4.2.3.text: At Makola market, 3 kg of rice costs GH₵ 54. What is the cost of 1 kg? Use this rate to find the cost of 5 kg and of 12 kg.
On a map of Ghana, 1 cm stands for 50 km. Tamale and Bolgatanga are about 3 cm apart on the map. About how far apart are the two towns?
Adongo draws a plan of his classroom in Bongo with a scale of 1 : 100. On the plan the room is 8 cm long and 6 cm wide. What are the real length and width in metres?

math:B6.2.1.1.4.text: Kwame in Akim Oda makes a row of squares with matchsticks: 4 sticks for 1 square, 7 for 2 and 10 for 3. He predicts 16 sticks for 5 squares. Draw or build the pattern to check. Is he right?
Pupils in Paga set out bottle tops in triangle shapes using 1, then 3, then 6, then 10 tops. Predict the number of tops in the 6th shape. Draw the shapes to check your answer.
Adinkra stamps on a cloth at Ntonso follow a pattern: row 1 has 2 stamps, row 2 has 5 and row 3 has 8. Predict the number of stamps in row 7, then sketch the rows to check.

math:B6.2.1.1.7.text: A taxi in Takoradi charges GH₵ 5 to start plus GH₵ 3 for each kilometre. Trips of 1, 2 and 3 km cost GH₵ 8, GH₵ 11 and GH₵ 14. Write the rule for a trip of n km in words and in algebra.
Bags of charcoal are stacked by the road at Buipe: 6 in the first row, 12 in the second and 18 in the third. Write the rule for row n in words and as an algebra expression.
Asibi in Bawku starts with 40 guinea fowl eggs and sells 4 each day. After days 1, 2 and 3 she has 36, 32 and 28 eggs. Write a rule in words and in algebra for the eggs left after day n.

math:B6.2.1.1.8.text: A price table at a canteen in Akosombo shows jollof: 1 bowl GH₵ 12, 2 bowls GH₵ 24, 3 bowls GH₵ 36. Write an expression for the cost of n bowls. How many bowls cost GH₵ 180?
An okada rider in Damongo keeps a table: 2 trips earn GH₵ 14, 3 trips earn GH₵ 21 and 5 trips earn GH₵ 35. Say how earnings change with trips. Write an expression for t trips.

A tank at Gushegu holds 500 litres. A table shows the water left as buckets are drawn. It is 480 litres after 1 bucket, 460 after 2 and 440 after 3. Write an expression for the litres left after b buckets.

math:B6.2.2.1.1.text: A ball of kenkey costs k cedis at Chorkor and a fried fish costs GH₵ 10 more than that. Write an expression for the price of the fish. Write another for 3 balls of kenkey and 1 fish.
Naa Adjeley sells mangoes at Madina market. She sells m in the morning, m + 4 in the afternoon and 2m in the evening. Write the total as one expression and simplify it.
A trotro fare is t cedis and a taxi fare is x cedis. In one week Edem of Anloga pays 5t + 2x. Find how much he pays when t = 6 and x = 15.

math:B6.2.3.1.2.text: Ekow in Anomabo had some oranges. After he bought 14 more he had 41. Let x be the number he had at first. Write an equation for this story and solve it.
Four friends in Bole share the cost of a football equally and each pays GH₵ 35. Let c be the cost of the ball. Write an equation with c and solve it.
Six bowls of koko cost GH₵ 30 at a stall in Nima. Let p be the price of one bowl. Write an equation and find the value of p.

math:B6.2.3.1.3.text: Make up a story about buying waakye at a stall in Dansoman that fits the equation 3w = 45. Say what w stands for, then solve the equation.
Write two different stories for the equation x - 12 = 30. One can be about mangoes on a tree in Yeji and the other about riders on a trotro. Solve it to check that your stories make sense.
Tell a story about sharing groundnuts among 5 friends in Gambaga that fits the equation n ÷ 5 = 8. What does n stand for? Find n.

math:B6.3.1.1.1.text: In a shop at Dunkwa-on-Offin, Serwaa sees a box of matches, a tin of milk, a football and a carton of soap. Which of these are rectangular prisms? What shape is the cross-section of each prism?
A long bar of washing soap from Konongo market is cut straight across in three places. What shape is each cut face? Is it the same each time? What does this tell you about the shape of the bar?
The roof space of a house in Aburi looks like a triangle from the front and keeps that shape all the way to the back. What 3D shape is it? Name the shapes of its faces.

math:B6.3.1.1.2.text: Open up an empty carton from a shop in Tarkwa and lay it flat. How many rectangles are in its net? Draw the net on card, cut it out and fold it back into a rectangular prism.
Narteh in Somanya wants a card box for beads that is 8 cm long, 6 cm wide and 4 cm high. Draw its net with tabs, cut it out and fold it. What are the sizes of its six faces?
Make a model tent for a class display in Sandema: a triangular prism 12 cm long whose ends are triangles with 6 cm sides. Draw the net. How many triangles and rectangles does it need?

math:B6.3.3.5.1.text: On a map of Ghana, find Accra and Ho. Is Ho to the north-east or to the north-west of Accra? In which direction do you travel to go from Ho back to Accra?
On a grid map of a village near Nalerigu, the school is 3 squares east and 3 squares north of Wuni's house. In which direction is the school from his house? And his house from the school?

Adzo starts at the chief's palace on a grid map of a town near Dambai. She goes 2 squares west and 2 squares south to the market. In which direction is the market from the palace? Describe the way back.

math:B6.3.3.6.1.text: On squared paper, draw the sail of a fishing canoe at Elmina as a triangle with corners (1, 1), (4, 1) and (1, 5). Reflect it in the y-axis. Write the corners of the image.
A kente weaver at Bonwire repeats a square shape by sliding it 5 squares right and 2 squares down on a grid. Write this slide as a translation vector. Where does the corner at (1, 4) move to?
Suhuyini in Kumbungu draws a flag shape 2 squares to the left of a mirror line on squared paper and reflects it. Where is the image? Are its size and shape the same as the flag?

math:B6.3.3.6.2.text: On a kente strip from Agotime Kpetoe, shape B looks like shape A flipped over a line. Shape C looks like A moved along without turning. Which one is a reflection and which is a translation? How can you tell?
A floor tile design in Cape Coast has triangle P at (2, 1), (4, 1), (2, 3) and triangle Q at (2, -1), (4, -1), (2, -3). Is Q a reflection or a translation of P? Name the mirror line or the vector.
Nyameke in Esiama moves a square with corners (0, 0), (2, 0), (2, 2), (0, 2) to (3, -4), (5, -4), (5, -2), (3, -2). Which single transformation is this? Write its vector.

math:B6.4.1.1.1.text: Ama in Sunyani takes the temperature in the school yard. It is 24°C at 7 a.m., 27°C at 9 a.m., 31°C at 11 a.m., 33°C at 1 p.m. and 30°C at 3 p.m. Choose a title, axes and a scale. Draw a line graph.
A school tank in Wechiau held 900 litres on Monday, then 750, 600, 480 and 300 litres on the next four days. Pick a scale for each axis, add a title and draw a line graph.
At a clinic in Agona Swedru, Kwabena's baby brother weighed 4 kg, 5 kg, 5.5 kg, 6.5 kg and 7 kg in months 1 to 5. What goes on each axis? What scale fits? Draw the line graph.

math:B6.4.1.1.2.text: Mawusi in Kadjebi measures the height of her maize plant every day. Lamisi in Karaga counts the pupils in each class. Whose data is continuous and suits a line graph? Explain why.
A station master at Kaneshie counts the trotros that leave each hour. Can 7.5 trotros leave? Should the points on his graph be joined with a line? Give a reason.
A farmer in Pusiga weighs a growing goat each week. A Berekum team counts its goals in each match. Which data set is continuous and which is discrete? Which one should be drawn as a joined line?

math:B6.4.1.1.3.text: A class in Kumasi recorded rainfall in mm: March 140, April 150, May 190, June 230, July 130, August 80. Draw a line graph. Which month was wettest? Between which two months did rain drop most?
A kiosk in Hohoe sold 20, 35, 30, 50, 65 and 80 bottles of water from Monday to Saturday. Draw a line graph. On which day did sales fall? What does the graph tell you about the week?
A tuber of yam at Kintampo market cost GH₵ 30 in March, GH₵ 28 in May, GH₵ 20 in July, GH₵ 15 in September and GH₵ 18 in November. Draw a line graph. When was yam cheapest? Suggest why.

math:B6.4.1.2.1.text: Your class in Mampong must choose a drink for the end-of-term party: sobolo, asaana or fruit juice. Would you use a questionnaire, an interview or observation to find out? Give a reason.
A head teacher in Kpandai wants to know how many pupils come to school on foot, by bicycle or by okada. Would you watch at the gate or hand out a question form? Explain your choice.
You need the total rainfall in Wa for each month of last year. Would you measure it yourself, interview a farmer or look up weather records? Say which is best and why.

math:B6.4.1.2.2.text: Write five questions to find out how pupils in your class in Sefwi Bekwai get to school and how much they pay for trotro or okada each day. Ask ten classmates and record their answers in a table.
Design a short question form on favourite foods such as fufu, banku, tuo zaafi and waakye. Use it with 12 pupils in your school. Record each pupil's answers in one row of a table.
Your class in Nandom wants to know which game pupils play most: ampe, oware, football or chaskele. Write the questions, choose whom to ask, collect the answers and record them neatly.

math:B6.4.1.2.3.text: A class in Asamankese asked 30 pupils to pick a fruit for break time: orange 12, mango 9, banana 6, pawpaw 3. Make a frequency table, draw a bar graph and say which fruit the school should buy most.
Abiba's group in Tolon asked 24 pupils their shoe size for sports shoes: 6 wear size 5, 10 wear size 6 and 8 wear size 7. Draw a bar graph. How many pairs of each size are needed for 48 pupils?
Plan a survey for a class food sale in Sogakope: kelewele, bofrot or roasted groundnuts? Ask 25 pupils, tally the answers, draw a bar graph and write down what your class should sell.

math:B6.4.2.2.1.text: Before a football match in Dormaa Ahenkro, the referee tosses a 50 pesewas coin. List all the possible outcomes. What is the probability that the coin lands on heads?
Ludo is played in many homes in Bekwai. List all the outcomes when the die is rolled once. What is the probability of rolling a 6? Of rolling a number greater than 4?
Delali in Denu tosses a 20 pesewas coin 50 times. It shows heads 27 times. Write the experimental probability of heads as a fraction. Is it more or less than the theoretical one?

math:B6.4.2.2.2.text: A spinner at a school fun fair in Drobo has 8 equal parts numbered 1 to 8. What is the probability of landing on a number greater than 5? In 80 spins, about how many times would you expect this?
A bag at a kiosk in Prampram holds 5 toffees of the same size: 2 red, 2 yellow and 1 green. Ayeley picks one without looking. Predict the probability that it is red. Which colour is least likely?

Atanga in Tongo makes a spinner with 5 equal parts named kenkey, banku, fufu, waakye and jollof. What is the probability that it stops on banku or fufu? Predict the number of such results in 100 spins.

math:B6.4.2.2.3.text: Six groups in Agogo each toss a GH₵ 1 coin 20 times and get 8, 13, 9, 12, 11 and 7 heads. Find each group's fraction of heads, then the fraction for all 120 tosses. Which is closer to 1/2? Why?
Esinam in Akatsi rolls a ludo die 12 times and gets only one 6. After 600 rolls she has 97 sixes. Compare 1/12 and 97/600 with the theoretical 1/6. What happens as the number of rolls grows?
Kwaku in Nkoranza says, 'I tossed a coin 4 times and got 4 heads, so heads always wins.' Explain why 4 tosses are too few. About how many heads would you expect in 1,000 tosses?

1:lower: Count the oranges Auntie Esi stacks in piles at her market stall, then count on as she adds more.
Share 12 groundnuts equally between 3 friends after school. How many does each friend get?
Use 1 cedi and 2 cedi coins to make 5 cedis in as many ways as you can.
1:upper: A cocoa farm in the Western Region harvested 2,480 kg this season. Read the number aloud, write it in words, then round it to the nearest hundred.
Kofi buys kenkey for GH₵ 7.50 and fried fish for GH₵ 12.00 and pays with a GH₵ 50 note. How much change does he get?
Ama's mother cuts a pineapple into 8 equal slices and sells 3. What fraction of the pineapple is left?
2:lower: A kente strip repeats gold, green, gold, green. Which colour comes next? Make your own repeating pattern with bottle tops.
In a game of ampe, the jumps go left, right, left, right. Clap the pattern and say what comes tenth.
2:upper: A trotro charges GH₵ 3 for each stop. Make a table of fares for 1 to 6 stops and write the rule.
Yaw saves GH₵ 2 every school day. Write a number sentence for how much he has after n days.
3:lower: Find circles, squares and triangles in Adinkra symbols printed on cloth at home.
Measure two sticks of sugarcane with hand spans. Which one is longer, and by how many spans?
Which holds more water: a sachet of pure water or a cup? Pour and compare.
3:upper: Measure the school garden bed with a rope and a metre stick, then work out its perimeter.
A piece of kente is 4 squares long and 3 squares wide. How many squares cover it?
A bus leaves Kumasi at 9:15 am and reaches Accra at 2:45 pm. How long is the journey?
4:lower: Ask your classmates their favourite food: jollof, waakye, banku or fufu. Record the answers with tally marks.
Count the goats, sheep and chickens you pass on the way to school and show them in a picture graph.
4:upper: Record how many days it rains in your town this month and draw a bar graph of each week.
Toss a bottle top 20 times. Predict how often it lands face up, then compare with what happens.
Survey your class on how they get to school (walking, trotro, okada, car) and find the most common way.
